domains.label: Mathematics & optimization
domains.description: Mathematical constructions, inequalities, generic optimizers and numerical algorithms.
domains.why_it_matters: Candidate objects or algorithms can improve explicit bounds, feasibility, approximation error or search efficiency.

domains.label: Operations research
domains.description: Routing, packing, scheduling, allocation and constraint models with an operational objective.
domains.why_it_matters: These tasks study how to use limited space, time and resources under explicit constraints.

domains.label: Machine learning & language
domains.description: Learning algorithms, generic prediction, language benchmarks, retrieval and digital-agent behavior.
domains.why_it_matters: Compare generalization, reasoning, learning procedures and retrieval quality across defined data and benchmark tasks.

domains.label: Software engineering
domains.description: Program synthesis, code repair, repository tasks and verification workflows.
domains.why_it_matters: Correctness and task completion expose whether generated software satisfies a program or repository contract.

domains.label: Computer systems & hardware
domains.description: Kernels, compilers, databases, datacenters, circuits and infrastructure optimization.
domains.why_it_matters: Latency, throughput, resource use and hardware constraints connect candidate programs to computing efficiency.

domains.label: Robotics & control
domains.description: Feedback controllers, embodied policies and rewards for locomotion or manipulation.
domains.why_it_matters: Closed-loop behavior tests stability, task completion and control performance, often in simulation.

domains.label: Physics
domains.description: Physical models, cosmology, quantum systems, transport, event reconstruction and physical-law inference.
domains.why_it_matters: Compare physical constructions, inferred relationships and numerical methods against declared measurements or simulations.

domains.label: Chemistry & materials
domains.description: Reaction kinetics, chemical transformations, material properties and constitutive models.
domains.why_it_matters: Infer stress–strain relationships, integrate chemical reaction dynamics and predict reaction outcomes or material properties.

domains.label: Biology & health
domains.description: Growth, biological sequences, cellular or neural data and biological or medical prediction targets.
domains.why_it_matters: Fit growth and population models, analyze RNA and cellular data, and learn predictive relationships in biological imagery and neural activity.

domains.label: Earth & environment
domains.description: Earth-system and environmental models, observations, prediction and resource-control targets.
domains.why_it_matters: Modeling environmental observations can test forecasting or process prediction under a defined dataset protocol.

domains.label: Finance & economics
domains.description: Economic decisions, allocation, mechanism design, structural models and financial policies.
domains.why_it_matters: Study economic models and decision rules under explicit objectives, information limits and feasibility constraints.

domains.label: Mixed / unclassified
domains.description: The available metadata describes a mixed suite or does not identify one primary application domain.
domains.why_it_matters: Keep mixed or underspecified packages visible while more detailed target and evaluation evidence is recorded.

task_types.label: Mathematical construction
task_types.description: Construct a discrete or continuous object under mathematical constraints.
task_types.why_it_matters: Feasibility and an explicit extremal objective make candidate configurations directly comparable.

task_types.label: Combinatorial optimization
task_types.description: Design a constructive heuristic or search strategy for a discrete allocation problem.
task_types.why_it_matters: Solution quality and feasibility measure how a method navigates a constrained search space.

task_types.label: Black-box optimization
task_types.description: Design an optimizer, acquisition function or selection policy for an objective oracle.
task_types.why_it_matters: Evaluation budgets and attained objective values test search efficiency rather than one fixed solution.

task_types.label: Symbolic regression
task_types.description: Recover an equation, scaling law or symbolic-regression procedure from data.
task_types.why_it_matters: Held-out error tests whether a compact functional expression predicts beyond the fitted examples.

task_types.label: Numerical solver
task_types.description: Integrate or simulate specified dynamics, solve equations, or design numerical integration and sampling procedures.
task_types.why_it_matters: Accuracy and numerical cost quantify behavior on specified functions, states or trajectories.

task_types.label: Prediction & model design
task_types.description: Fit, infer, train or design a predictive or generative model, representation or parameter estimate.
task_types.why_it_matters: Prediction error or task return evaluates learned behavior on the declared data or environment.

task_types.label: Hyperparameter search
task_types.description: Optimize training settings or model hyperparameters.
task_types.why_it_matters: A held-out objective tests the quality and cost of selecting a model configuration.

task_types.label: Language & reasoning
task_types.description: Optimize prompts, scaffolds or outputs on language, reasoning or grid-inference benchmarks.
task_types.why_it_matters: Measure compositional reasoning, language understanding and constraint satisfaction on specified benchmark cases.

task_types.label: Agent workflow
task_types.description: Design an agent workflow for tools, web environments, planning or digital tasks.
task_types.why_it_matters: End-to-end task completion tests how actions and tools are coordinated across a trajectory.

task_types.label: Software generation & repair
task_types.description: Generate, repair, review or verify program code.
task_types.why_it_matters: Executable tests or repository task outcomes connect a proposed change to software behavior.

task_types.label: Systems optimization
task_types.description: Improve kernel, compiler, infrastructure, hardware or program-performance decisions.
task_types.why_it_matters: Correctness plus cost or performance measurements test whether systems changes are useful.

task_types.label: Control policy
task_types.description: Design a feedback controller, sequential decision rule or embodied action policy.
task_types.why_it_matters: Sequential outcomes test decisions under changing state and information constraints.

task_types.label: Reward design
task_types.description: Design a reward for a learning controller or policy.
task_types.why_it_matters: The resulting trained behavior tests whether the reward induces the intended task behavior.

task_types.label: Information retrieval
task_types.why_it_matters: Relevance measurements compare ranking functions and document-search quality across different collections.

task_types.label: Constraint modeling
task_types.description: Reformulate or solve explicit satisfiability, logic or mathematical-program constraints.
task_types.why_it_matters: Feasibility and solver efficiency expose the value of the model formulation or solver policy.

task_types.label: Benchmark generation
task_types.description: Generate benchmark functions or embodied evaluation tasks.
task_types.why_it_matters: Produce controlled instances for probing evaluation coverage, difficulty and optimizer or policy robustness.

task_types.label: Signal processing
task_types.description: Filter or transform a signal under error, noise and smoothness criteria.
task_types.why_it_matters: Output fidelity and robustness test whether useful signal structure survives processing.

task_types.label: Unclassified task type
task_types.description: The catalog does not yet specify a clear candidate or evaluation operation.
task_types.why_it_matters: Expose gaps in the recorded optimization contract so future catalog curation can resolve them.

coverage.label: Executable definitions
coverage.description: Packages with source-declared executable evaluators; environments and runtime are not verified by Arena.

coverage.label: Unsupported definitions
coverage.description: Catalogued packages whose source marks evaluation unsupported; they remain included in domain totals.

coverage.label: Original protocol
coverage.description: Source labels the evaluator protocol original; this is not Arena conformance or runtime verification.

coverage.label: Source-declared verified reconstruction
coverage.description: Source labels these reconstructions verified. Arena has not independently rerun that verification.

coverage.label: Recreated protocol
coverage.description: Recreated evaluators without the source's recreated_verified designation.

coverage.label: Recorded I/O contract
coverage.description: Non-null problem.json contract text; may point to evaluator documentation rather than a complete machine-readable signature.

coverage.label: Arena runtime verification recorded
coverage.description: No package in this pinned catalog carries Arena runtime verification. This does not mean its evaluator fails.

science-acyclic-vertex-coloring.rationale: The candidate assigns a colour to each vertex of a fixed 50-vertex circulant graph. The evaluator checks that the colouring is proper and that every two colour classes induce a forest, and counts the colours used. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_655, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Few colors without any bicolored cycle
evidence.description: construct() -> fifty Python integer color labels in 0..49 for the pinned degree-four graph. Adjacent vertices must differ and the subgraph induced by any two colors must be a forest. Minimize number of distinct colors; union-find detects bicolored cycles exactly. A fixed 50-vertex degree-four circulant graph with steps 1 and 7 is colored. A lower score is a better finite coloring, not a new general maximum-degree bound.

science-additive-two-basis-212.rationale: The candidate returns a set of integers in 0..212; the evaluator checks exactly that every integer 0..212 is a sum of two elements and scores the set size. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_additive_basis, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Smallest set whose pairwise sums cover 0..212
evidence.description: construct() -> distinct integers in 0..212 such that every integer 0..212 equals a + b for some a <= b in the set (a = b allowed). Minimize the size; the optimum is 25. For n = 212 the minimum is 25, so the task recovers an extremal basis.

science-algebra-sparse-polynomial-square.rationale: The candidate returns the integer coefficients of a 12-term polynomial of degree at most 40 with entries in [-64, 64]; the evaluator squares it exactly and counts the nonzero coefficients of the square, which is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_sparse_polynomial_square, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Sparse squares of twelve-term integer polynomials
evidence.description: Return coefficient list in ascending degree, length<=41, nonzero final coefficient, entries integers in [-64,64], exactly 12 nonzero terms. Minimize nonzero terms in the EXACT integer square. Restricts the characteristic-zero polynomial problem to bounded integer coefficients and degree; cancellation is exact and no general lower-bound theorem is claimed.

science-all-progression-discrepancy-256.rationale: The candidate assigns a sign of -1 or +1 to each of the integers 1 to 256; the evaluator computes exactly the largest absolute signed sum over every arithmetic progression in that interval, which is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_progression_discrepancy, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Low discrepancy on all arithmetic progressions
evidence.description: construct() -> exactly n=256 Python integer signs -1 or +1. Minimize the maximum absolute signed sum on ANY arithmetic progression contained in [1,256], any start, positive step and length including one. Assign 256 signs and minimize the maximum absolute sum on any arithmetic progression, including arbitrary starts and singletons. This differs from homogeneous-progression Erdős discrepancy.

science-anti-ramsey-four-cycle-colors-16.rationale: The candidate colours the edges of the complete graph on 16 vertices. The evaluator checks that no four-cycle has four distinct colours and scores the number of colours used. Reviewed source family science_prize_d_rainbow_c4_avoidance, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Many edge colors without a rainbow four-cycle
evidence.description: construct() -> 120 integer colors in 0..119 for the lexicographically ordered pairs (i,j), 0<=i<j<16. No four-cycle may have four distinct edge colors. Maximize the number of colors actually used; all three cycles on every four-vertex subset are checked. The n=16, cycle-length-four task searches extremal colorings for a solved finite specialization, using an independently written exhaustive verifier.

science-b2-2-sets-1000.rationale: The candidate constructs a set of distinct integers in 1..1000; the evaluator counts the representations a + b (a <= b) of every sum exactly, requires at most two per sum and scores the size of the set. Reviewed source family science_prize_i_b2_2_sets, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large subsets of {1, ..., 1000} in which every sum has at most two representations (B2[2] sets)
evidence.description: construct() -> distinct integers in 1..1000 such that every integer has at most two representations a + b with a <= b from the set (exact count). Maximize the size. Sizes for N = 1000 are finite lower bounds for the extremal function (the asymptotic constant is at least 3/2); no finite optimum is documented.

science-biology-balibase-protein-alignme.rationale: The candidate aligns the unaligned protein sequences of 26 BAliBASE test cases. The evaluator checks that each alignment is a gapped version of the inputs and scores the sum-of-pairs agreement with the structure-based reference on its core blocks. Reviewed source family biology_research_balibase_alignment, area biology.

evidence.task_name: Biology: protein multiple-alignment accuracy on BAliBASE reference alignments
evidence.description: Align the unaligned protein sequences of 26 BAliBASE reference-1 test cases, spanning very divergent and medium-divergence families. The evaluator checks that each alignment is a valid gapped version of the input sequences and scores the sum-of-pairs agreement with the structure-based reference alignment on its annotated core blocks.

evidence.description: Reconstruct microbial contigs from CAMI-derived reads and score genome recovery with independent reference-aware misassembly and sequence-error penalties.

evidence.description: Decode physically mass-consistent peptide sequences from measured fragment spectra and rank confidence under exact-sequence and precision-coverage evaluation.

evidence.description: Search for RNA sequences whose independently evaluated minimum-free-energy structures match Eterna100-v2 targets under a folding-call budget.

science-biology-fmd-microscopy-denoising.rationale: The candidate denoises fluorescence microscopy measurements; image fidelity is a biological-imaging signal-processing target. Reviewed source family science_biology_b09, area biology.

evidence.description: Recover calibrated fluorescence intensities from real noisy acquisitions, using averaged acquired exposures as imperfect reference images.

science-biology-gears-perturbation.rationale: The candidate estimates biological effects, parameters, sequences, networks or cellular structure from the named biological data. evidence.description: Predict expression shifts for complete held-out genetic perturbations using measured GEARS study pseudobulks and training-only gene selection.

science-biology-hp-lattice-folding-2d.rationale: The candidate is a folding routine that returns self-avoiding square-lattice conformations for ten HP benchmark sequences within a CPU budget. The evaluator rechecks each walk, recomputes its hydrophobic contact energy and scores the mean ratio to literature reference energies. Reviewed source family biology_research_hp_square_lattice, area biology.

evidence.task_name: Biology: HP lattice protein folding on the square lattice
evidence.description: Fold the ten standard two-dimensional HP benchmark sequences (20 to 100 residues) into low-energy self-avoiding conformations on the square lattice. The evaluator checks self-avoidance, recomputes the hydrophobic contact energy of every conformation and scores the mean ratio to the lowest energies reported in the literature.

science-biology-hp-lattice-folding-3d.rationale: The candidate is a folding routine that returns self-avoiding cubic-lattice conformations for sixteen HP benchmark chains within a CPU budget. The evaluator rechecks each walk, recomputes its hydrophobic contact energy and scores the mean ratio to literature reference energies. Reviewed source family biology_research_hp_cubic_lattice, area biology.

evidence.task_name: Biology: HP lattice protein folding on the cubic lattice
evidence.description: Fold the sixteen standard three-dimensional HP benchmark chains (the ten 48-residue sequences with proven ground states plus six longer chains of 64 to 136 residues) on the simple cubic lattice. The evaluator checks self-avoidance, recomputes every hydrophobic contact energy and scores the mean ratio to the published reference energies.

science-biology-influenza-hospitalizatio.rationale: The candidate issues weekly quantile forecasts of influenza hospital admissions one to four weeks ahead for each US state through a held-out season. The evaluator scores the mean weighted interval score against the reported admissions. Reviewed source family biology_research_influenza_hospitalizations, area biology.

evidence.task_name: Biology: probabilistic forecasts of state influenza hospital admissions
evidence.description: Issue weekly quantile forecasts of laboratory-confirmed influenza hospital admissions one to four weeks ahead for every US state through the held-out 2024-2025 season, seeing only the surveillance history up to each forecast week. The evaluator scores the quantiles with the weighted interval score used by the CDC FluSight hub.

evidence.description: Infer steady-state reaction fluxes and uncertainty intervals from isotope measurements using a verified source-specific atom-mapping forward model.

evidence.description: Fit mechanistic biochemical ODE parameters from measured signaling trajectories and predict complete held-out stimulation conditions with an independent source-model solver.

science-biology-phylogenetic-likelihood.rationale: The candidate constructs a valid phylogenetic tree and branch parameters; the evaluator recomputes likelihood on a DNA alignment. Reviewed source family science_biology_b07, area biology.

evidence.task_name: Biology: Empirical phylogenetic tree likelihood search
evidence.description: Construct a valid evolutionary tree for an empirical DNA alignment; an independently written pruning evaluator recomputes its JC69 likelihood.

science-biology-phylogeny-topology-recov.rationale: The candidate reconstructs tree topologies from DNA sequences simulated along hidden trees. evidence.task_name: Biology: phylogenetic topology recovery from simulated sequences
evidence.description: Reconstruct the unrooted tree topology of twenty simulated instances with 8 to 32 taxa and 250 to 2000 sites, generated inside the evaluator under the Jukes-Cantor model with hidden random topologies and branch lengths. evidence.description: Fit a mutation-effect model from measured support substitutions and predict complete held-out mutation positions in three ProteinGym assays.

science-biology-rna-secondary-structure.rationale: The candidate predicts a dot-bracket secondary structure for each of 90 non-coding RNA sequences. evidence.task_name: Biology: RNA secondary-structure prediction against Rfam consensus structures
evidence.description: Predict the secondary structure of 90 non-coding RNA sequences from 47 Rfam families that have experimentally determined three-dimensional structures. The evaluator compares the predicted base pairs with the family's consensus pairing projected onto each sequence and scores the mean F1.

science-biology-spatial-deconvolution.rationale: The candidate estimates biological effects, parameters, sequences, networks or cellular structure from the named biological data. Its modeling operation does not make the primary domain generic ML. Reviewed source family science_biology_b06, area biology.

evidence.task_name: Biology: Spatial transcriptomic cell abundance inference
evidence.description: Infer nonnegative spatial cell counts from reference expression signatures and evaluate separate held-out genes using a count likelihood.

science-bounded-additive-basis-multiplic.rationale: The candidate constructs a subset of [0,128] whose pairwise sums cover every integer in [128,256]; the evaluator verifies the coverage and counts representations exactly, and the largest count is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_bounded_basis, area mathematics.

evidence.description: construct() -> a nonempty subset A of [0,n=128]. Every integer in [128,256] must be a sum of two elements of A. Pair representations are unordered and permit equal summands. Minimize the largest representation multiplicity in that target interval. Choose A in [0,128] covering [128,256] by pair sums and minimize peak multiplicity. Local pairs are unordered and include equal summands; the paper’s ordered convention differs by symmetry.

science-cardinality-separated-subset-sum.rationale: The candidate returns a set of integers in 1..256. The evaluator checks by exact dynamic programming that subsets of different sizes never have equal sums and scores the set size. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_725, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large sets with cardinality-separated subset sums
evidence.description: construct() -> 1..60 distinct integers in 1..256. Whenever two subsets have different cardinalities their sums must differ. Repeated sums within the SAME cardinality are allowed. The empty subset is included. Maximize set size using exact cardinality-indexed subset-sum dynamic programming. N=256 with at most sixty output members is a bounded finite instance. This is weaker than requiring all subset sums distinct and is intentionally a different task. No optimality or infinite-density conclusion follows.

science-chemistry-adme-mdr1-efflux-bioge.rationale: The candidate fits a model on the training molecules of one Biogen ADME endpoint and predicts the held-out molecules from their SMILES in a separate process; the evaluator scores the mean absolute error against labels the candidate never receives. Reviewed source family science_chemistry_biogen_adme, area chemistry.

evidence.task_name: ADME: MDR1-MDCK efflux ratio (Biogen public set)
evidence.description: Predict the MDR1-MDCK efflux ratio (log10 of B-A over A-B permeability) of 529 test compounds from 2113 training compounds measured in the same Biogen assay. The evaluator scores the mean absolute error on the authors' official test split.

science-chemistry-adme-microsomal-cleara.rationale: The candidate fits a model on the training molecules of one Biogen ADME endpoint and predicts the held-out molecules from their SMILES in a separate process; the evaluator scores the mean absolute error against labels the candidate never receives. evidence.description: Predict the human liver microsomal intrinsic clearance (log10 mL/min/kg) of 618 test compounds from 2469 training compounds measured in the same Biogen assay. The evaluator scores the mean absolute error on the authors' official test split.

science-chemistry-adme-rat-microsomal-cl.rationale: The candidate fits a model on the training molecules of one Biogen ADME endpoint and predicts the held-out molecules from their SMILES in a separate process; the evaluator scores the mean absolute error against labels the candidate never receives.
