science-chemistry-buchwald-hartwig-yield.rationale: The candidate predicts yields of Buchwald-Hartwig couplings whose additives never occur in training, on four published out-of-sample tests. The evaluator scores the mean coefficient of determination against withheld yields. Reviewed source family science_chemistry_buchwald_hartwig_yield, area chemistry.

evidence.task_name: Buchwald-Hartwig yield prediction for unseen additives
evidence.description: Predict the yields of palladium-catalysed C-N couplings that use isoxazole additives never seen in training, on the four out-of-sample tests of Ahneman et al. The evaluator scores the mean coefficient of determination (R^2) over the four tests.

science-chemistry-lennard-jones-38.rationale: The candidate constructs atomic coordinates or molecular conformations under geometric and chemical constraints, evaluated through the declared energy or structural objective. Reviewed source family science_lj_cluster, area chemistry.

evidence.description: Place 38 atoms interacting through the Lennard-Jones potential (reduced units) to minimise the total energy. LJ38 is the classic hard case of cluster optimisation: the global minimum is a face-centred-cubic truncated octahedron (energy -173.928427, Cambridge Cluster Database) while the icosahedral funnel traps local searches. The evaluator computes the energy exactly; the seed is a cubic lattice fragment.

science-chemistry-lennard-jones-55.rationale: The candidate constructs atomic coordinates or molecular conformations under geometric and chemical constraints, evaluated through the declared energy or structural objective. Reviewed source family science_lj_cluster, area chemistry.

evidence.description: Place 55 atoms interacting through the Lennard-Jones potential to minimise the total energy. The global minimum is the complete two-shell Mackay icosahedron (energy -279.248470, Cambridge Cluster Database). The evaluator computes the energy exactly; the seed is a cubic lattice fragment.

science-chemistry-mmff94-drug-conformers.rationale: The candidate returns atomic coordinates of eight drug molecules that keep connectivity and stereochemistry. The evaluator recomputes the MMFF94 energy of each geometry and scores the mean energy above stored reference minima. Reviewed source family science_chemistry_mmff_conformers, area chemistry.

evidence.task_name: Lowest-energy MMFF94 conformers of eight drug molecules
evidence.description: Find, for each of eight flexible drug molecules, the conformer with the lowest MMFF94 force-field energy while keeping the molecule's connectivity and stereochemistry. The evaluator recomputes the energy of the returned coordinates and compares it with minima from an extensive reference search.

science-chemistry-morse-cluster-minima.rationale: The candidate constructs atomic coordinates of six Morse clusters with 38 to 80 atoms. The evaluator recomputes each energy and scores the mean relative excess over tabulated putative minima. Reviewed source family science_chemistry_morse_clusters, area chemistry.

evidence.task_name: Morse cluster global minima across the range of the potential
evidence.description: Find the lowest-energy arrangements of 38 to 80 atoms bound by Morse potentials of long, medium and short range (six instances). Energies are recomputed exactly and compared with the putative global minima of Doye and Wales.

science-chemistry-suzuki-miyaura-yield-r.rationale: The candidate predicts yields of Suzuki-Miyaura couplings on ten random 70/30 splits of a published screening dataset. The evaluator scores the mean coefficient of determination against withheld yields. Reviewed source family science_chemistry_suzuki_miyaura_yield, area chemistry.

evidence.task_name: Suzuki-Miyaura yield prediction on random splits
evidence.description: Predict the yields of 5760 Suzuki-Miyaura couplings screened by Perera et al. across electrophiles, nucleophiles, ligands, bases and solvents, on ten random 70/30 splits. The evaluator scores the mean coefficient of determination (R^2) over the splits.

science-chordal-clique-partition-instanc.rationale: The candidate returns a partition of the edges into cliques for each of three fixed seeded split graphs; the evaluator regenerates the graphs, checks that every listed set is a clique and every edge is covered exactly once, and scores the total number of cliques. Reviewed source family science_prize_i_chordal_clique_partition, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Clique partitions of three fixed split (chordal) graphs
evidence.description: construct() -> three lists of cliques (vertex lists), one per instance from split_graph(n, k, p, seed) for (30,10,0.7,301), (60,20,0.7,302), (90,30,0.7,303) in the verifier: a clique on the first k vertices, an independent set on the rest and each cross pair joined with probability p (split graphs are chordal). Every listed set must be a clique with at least two vertices and every edge must lie in exactly one listed clique. Minimize the total number of cliques; the Erdős-Ordman-Zalcstein question asks whether n^2/6 + O(n) always suffice, and split graphs need at most 3n^2/16 + O(n). The score totals clique partition sizes on three fixed random split graphs; it measures a partitioning method.

science-chowla-cosine-sixteen-frequencie.rationale: The candidate returns 16 distinct integer frequencies up to 200; the evaluator numerically minimizes the cosine sum over the circle (dense sampling with local refinement) and scores the minimum divided by 4, which is maximized. Reviewed source family science_prize_g_chowla, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Sixteen frequencies whose cosine sum stays shallow (Chowla's cosine problem)
evidence.description: construct() -> 16 distinct integers in 1..200. The score is min over theta of sum cos(a*theta), divided by sqrt(16), computed by dense sampling and bisection of every interval that a second-derivative bound cannot exclude (certified to about 1e-9). Maximize (make the minimum as shallow as possible). Shallow minima for 16 frequencies probe the finite side of Chowla's problem; no finite optimum is documented.

science-climate-lorenz96-assimilation.rationale: The source names a climate, hydrological, geophysical or environmental inference/forecasting target; its data may be simulated or measured as declared in the package. Reviewed source family science_lorenz_assimilation, area climate_dynamics.

evidence.description: Design an ensemble analysis update that reconstructs an evolving twenty-variable chaotic state from noisy observations of half its coordinates. The evaluator propagates the ensemble and compares each updated ensemble mean with independent high-accuracy reference trajectories.

science-climate-lorenz96-subgrid-closure.rationale: The candidate fits a shared polynomial closure for unresolved forcing in a synthetic climate-dynamics model; this is a bounded equation approximation, not an observed climate discovery. Reviewed source family science_lorenz_closure, area climate_dynamics.

evidence.description: Fit a shared degree-five polynomial approximation to the unresolved fast-scale forcing of a two-scale Lorenz-96 model. Train on supplied slow-state/tendency pairs and minimize normalized error on independent validation trajectories, including an unseen forcing regime.

science-clique-subdivision-certificate.rationale: The candidate returns branch vertices and internally disjoint connecting paths in a fixed 24-vertex graph. The evaluator checks that they form a subdivision of a complete graph and scores the number of branch vertices. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_585, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large clique subdivisions in a pinned graph
evidence.description: construct() -> {'branches': distinct vertices, 'paths': one simple path for each unordered pair of branches}. Path endpoints must be their branch pair; all path interiors must be pairwise disjoint and avoid every branch. All consecutive path vertices must be adjacent in the pinned graph. Maximize number of branch vertices. A local G(24,0.4) sample (random.Random(585)) is pinned. A certificate is a lower bound on this host’s largest subdivision order; no theorem about all chromatic graphs or reproduction of the paper’s proof is claimed.

science-clique-transversal-instances.rationale: The candidate returns a vertex set for each of three fixed seeded random graphs; the evaluator regenerates the graphs, enumerates all maximal cliques with at least two vertices, requires each to be hit and scores the total size of the sets. Reviewed source family science_prize_i_clique_transversal, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Small vertex sets meeting every maximal clique of three fixed random graphs
evidence.description: construct() -> three vertex lists, one per instance from random_graph(n, p, seed) for (30,0.3,201), (35,0.25,202), (40,0.2,203) in the verifier. Each list must meet every maximal clique with at least two vertices (all maximal cliques enumerated by Bron-Kerbosch). Minimize the total size. The score totals transversal sizes on three fixed random graphs; it measures a covering method. The exact optimum is 44 (12 + 13 + 19), which a minimum hitting-set search over the maximal cliques finds at once.

science-cluster-prime-difference-coverag.rationale: The candidate returns one prime at most 100000; the evaluator re-derives the primes and checks exactly that every even number up to p-3 is a difference of two primes at most p, and the prime is maximized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_cluster_prime, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Cluster primes with complete even-difference coverage
evidence.description: construct() -> a prime p with 3<=p<=maximum=100000. Every positive even d<=p-3 must be a difference of two primes <=p. The evaluator independently checks all differences. Maximize p. Maximize a cluster prime at most 100000; every even difference through p-3 is checked using primes at most p. No density theorem or infinity claim follows. The optimum is known, because OEIS A038134 lists every cluster prime below 10^5; this is a rediscovery task.

science-cochromatic-homogeneous-partitio.rationale: The candidate partitions the vertices of a fixed 14-vertex graph into parts that are each a clique or an independent set. The evaluator checks every part and counts the parts. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_506, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Cochromatic partitions of a pinned random graph
evidence.description: construct() -> partition of vertices 0..13 into nonempty lists. Every part must induce a clique or an independent set, and vertices occur exactly once. Minimize number of parts. The evaluator independently reports the exact ordinary chromatic number by subset dynamic programming. One explicit G(14,1/2) sample, generated locally with random.Random(506), is optimized. The candidate score is a cochromatic upper bound, not an asymptotic random-graph result or a guaranteed optimal partition.

science-common-vertex-edge-disjoint-cycl.rationale: The candidate lists edge-disjoint cycles on one common vertex set in a fixed 21-vertex circulant graph. The evaluator checks every cycle edge and counts the cycles. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_521, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Packing edge-disjoint cycles on one vertex set
evidence.description: construct() -> nonempty list of simple cycles, each represented by a list of distinct vertices with the closing edge implicit. All cycles must use exactly the same vertex set of size at least three in the pinned 21-vertex host. No host edge may occur in two cycles. Maximize number of cycles. The local task maximizes witness multiplicity in the explicit circulant host with steps 1, 2 and 5. This measures the finite cycle-packing quantity and cannot prove a universal chromatic forcing statement.

science-comparable-set-family-pairs.rationale: The candidate returns 40 distinct subsets of a 12-element set. The evaluator counts the pairs in which one set strictly contains the other. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_637, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Many comparable pairs in a fixed-size set family
evidence.description: construct() -> exactly forty distinct subsets of vertices 0..11, each as a list of distinct integers; the empty set is allowed. Maximize the number of unordered pairs in which one member is a strict subset of the other. The local parameters are n=12 and m=40. This is a finite lower-bound construction for c(12,40); the baseline consists of the first forty binary masks and does not copy the paper’s extremal constructions.

science-consecutive-primes-arithmetic-pr.rationale: The candidate returns a starting prime, a difference and a length; the evaluator verifies with deterministic primality tests that the terms are consecutive primes in arithmetic progression below 10^9 and scores the length. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_cpap, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Consecutive primes in arithmetic progression below 10^9
evidence.description: construct() -> [p, d, k] describing p, p + d, ..., p + (k-1)d with 2 <= k <= 64, 1 <= d <= 5000 and last term at most 10^9. Every term must be prime (deterministic Miller-Rabin) and no prime may lie strictly between consecutive terms. Maximize k; the optimum below 10^9 is 6. Below 10^9 the longest such progressions have six terms, so the task recovers a six-term progression.

science-consecutive-squarefree-gap.rationale: The candidate returns two squarefree integers at most 10^7 with no squarefree integer between them; the evaluator tests the endpoints and every interior integer exactly, and the gap is maximized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_squarefree_gap, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large gaps between consecutive squarefree integers
evidence.description: construct() -> [a,b], positive squarefree endpoints a<b<=maximum=10000000, with b-a<=10000. EVERY interior integer must be nonsquarefree. Maximize b-a. Endpoints and every interior integer are tested exactly. Maximize the gap between consecutive positive squarefree endpoints at most 10000000, with gap at most 10000. Endpoints and every interior integer are checked. The optimum is 10 (OEIS A020754); this is a rediscovery task.

science-consecutive-two-square-gap.rationale: The candidate returns two integers at most 10^7 that are sums of two squares with no such integer between them; the evaluator tests the endpoints and every interior integer exactly, and the gap is maximized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_two_square_gap, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large gaps between sums of two squares
evidence.description: construct() -> [a,b], positive endpoints a<b<=maximum=10000000, b-a<=10000, both sums of two integer squares (zero is permitted). No interior integer may be a sum of two squares. Maximize b-a. Positive consecutive representable endpoints at most 10000000 and distance at most 10000, with zero allowed as one of the two squared integers. Every interior integer is checked. The optimum is 50 (OEIS A297350); this is a rediscovery task.

science-coprime-abc-quality.rationale: The candidate returns a coprime triple a+b=c with c at most 10^12; the evaluator checks the equation and coprimality, factors the triple exactly, and scores log(c)/log(rad(abc)), which is maximized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_abc_quality, area mathematics.

evidence.description: construct() -> [a,b,c], positive Python integers <=1000000000000, a<=b, a+b=c, gcd(a,b)=1. Maximize log(c)/log(rad(a*b*c)). The radical is the product of DISTINCT prime factors and is independently factored exactly; only the logarithmic score uses floating arithmetic. Search coprime positive triples a+b=c with c<=10^12, maximizing log(c)/log(rad(abc)). Finite high quality cannot disprove the conjecture, which allows finitely many exceptions at each exponent. The optimum is quality 1.62991, attained by Reyssat's triple; complete tables of high-quality triples show nothing better below 10^20, so this is a rediscovery task.

science-coprime-adjacent-divisors.rationale: The candidate returns one integer up to 10^18; the evaluator factors it exactly, lists its divisors in increasing order and scores the number of adjacent divisor pairs that are coprime. Reviewed source family science_prize_i_coprime_divisors, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Integers up to 10^18 with many coprime adjacent divisors
evidence.description: construct() -> an integer n with 2 <= n <= 10^18. With the divisors of n in increasing order (exact factorization), the score tau_perp(n) is the number of adjacent pairs d_i < d_{i+1} with gcd 1. Maximize. Large values below 10^18 are finite lower-bound constructions for the maximal order of tau_perp.

science-coprime-reciprocal-distances-512.rationale: The candidate constructs a set of pairwise coprime integers below 512; the evaluator checks every pair for coprimality and scores the sum of 1/(512 - a) computed as an exact rational. Reviewed source family science_prize_i_coprime_reciprocals, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Pairwise coprime integers below 512 with large sum of 1/(512 - a)
evidence.description: construct() -> distinct pairwise coprime integers a in 1..511. The score is sum 1/(512 - a) (exact rational, reported as a float); the report also gives sum over primes p < 512 of 1/p. Maximize; the optimum is 2.762987911413. For n = 512 the maximum is 2.762987911413 (the prime reciprocal sum is 2.100662260951): every integer below 512 has at most one prime factor of 23 or more, so an exact dynamic programme over the subsets of the primes up to 19 solves the instance in milliseconds. The task recovers this value; it is one data point for the conjectured bound.

science-cosmology-dark-energy-growth-ind.rationale: The candidate fits a compact expansion-history or growth formula against cosmological observations or numerical references; the source distinguishes these settings. Reviewed source family science_cosmology_growth_index, area cosmology_and_astrophysics.

evidence.description: Improve a six-coefficient growth-index formula for the linear growth rate and normalized growth factor in smooth CPL dark-energy cosmologies. A tightly integrated general-relativistic second-order ODE provides an independent numerical reference. The score is the worst relative error across both observables on disjoint public validation cosmologies, extending the constant-gamma seed within a fixed compact ansatz.

science-cosmology-luminosity-distance-qu.rationale: The candidate specifies a quadrature rule or sampling schedule for a physical numerical calculation; accuracy is evaluated under the declared work constraints. Reviewed source family science_cosmology_distance_quadrature, area cosmology_and_astrophysics.

evidence.description: Discover an eight-node positive quadrature rule for dimensionless luminosity distance in spatially flat, time-varying dark-energy models. The same nodes and weights must work across all models. Minimize the worst relative error against independent adaptive integration on disjoint public validation cosmologies. This is a locally designed synthetic numerical-method task reconstructed from published distance and CPL equations.

science-cosmology-pantheon-plus-expansio.rationale: The candidate fits a compact expansion-history or growth formula against cosmological observations or numerical references; the source distinguishes these settings. Reviewed source family science_pantheon, area cosmology_and_astrophysics.

evidence.task_name: Expansion-history models fitted to the Pantheon+ supernova Hubble diagram
evidence.description: Propose a parametric expansion history E(z) = H(z)/H0 with at most six parameters and fit it to the 1,580 Pantheon+ Type Ia supernova light curves with zHD > 0.01 (the 1,590-object cosmology sample minus the ten Cepheid-host calibrators) (corrected apparent magnitudes and the full statistical plus systematic covariance). The absolute magnitude is profiled analytically; the score is the minimum chi-squared, lower is better. Flat LambdaCDM with a fitted matter density is reported for comparison.

science-cube-free-graphs-16.rationale: The candidate returns the edge list of a graph on 16 vertices; the evaluator searches exactly for a copy of the cube graph Q3 and scores the number of edges. Reviewed source family science_prize_f_cube_free, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Dense graphs on 16 vertices without the cube Q3
evidence.description: construct() -> list of edges [u, v] of a simple graph on vertices 0..15 containing no subgraph isomorphic to the 3-cube Q3 (exact search). Maximize the number of edges. A Q3-free graph with m edges certifies ex(16;Q3) >= m; no exact value for n = 16 is documented.

science-cycle-and-edge-decompositions.rationale: The candidate returns, for three fixed pseudo-random graphs, a partition of the edges into cycles and single edges; the evaluator checks that every edge is used exactly once and counts the pieces, fewer being better. Reviewed source family science_prize_f_cycle_decomposition, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Decompositions of three fixed graphs into few cycles and edges (Erdős-Gallai)
evidence.description: construct() -> three lists of pieces, one per fixed instance graph generated by instance_graph(n, p, seed) for (20,0.4,11), (25,0.35,12), (30,0.3,13) in the verifier. A piece is a single edge [u, v] or a cycle given by at least three distinct vertices (the closing edge is implied). Pieces must be edge-disjoint and cover all edges. Minimize the total number of pieces. The score counts pieces over three fixed random graphs; it measures decomposition algorithms, not the conjecture's constant.

science-cycle-length-spectra-10.rationale: The candidate returns up to 500 simple graphs on 10 vertices; the evaluator computes the set of cycle lengths of each graph exactly by dynamic programming over paths and scores the number of distinct sets. Reviewed source family science_prize_i_cycle_spectra, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Realizing every set of cycle lengths on 10 vertices
evidence.description: construct() -> a list of at most 500 simple graphs on vertices 0..9, each a list of edges [u, v]. The cycle set of a graph (the lengths of its cycles, computed exactly by dynamic programming over paths) is recorded for every graph. Maximize the number of distinct cycle sets; the optimum is 133. There are exactly 133 cycle sets on 10 vertices, so a complete collection recovers f(10).

science-cycle-plus-triangles-colouring.rationale: The candidate returns a 3-colouring for each of five fixed seeded cycle-plus-triangles graphs; the evaluator regenerates the graphs and scores the number of instances whose colouring is proper. Reviewed source family science_prize_i_cycle_plus_triangles, area mathematics.

evidence.description: construct() -> five colourings (one colour in {0, 1, 2} per vertex), one per instance from cycle_plus_triangles(n, seed) for n = 30, 60, 90, 150, 300 with seeds 401..405 in the verifier: the Hamiltonian cycle 0-1-...-(n-1)-0 plus a random partition into triangles avoiding cycle edges. The score is the number of properly coloured instances (0..5). Maximize; every instance is 3-colourable by the Fleischner-Stiebitz theorem. The score counts fixed instances coloured properly; it measures a constructive colouring method for graphs whose colourability is known only through an algebraic proof. On these five instances a standard min-conflicts local search already reaches the maximum 5 in under a second.

science-dense-clique-partition-instances.rationale: The candidate returns a partition of the edges into cliques for each of two fixed seeded dense random graphs; the evaluator regenerates the graphs, checks that every edge lies in exactly one listed clique and scores the total number of cliques. Reviewed source family science_prize_i_dense_clique_partition, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Clique partitions of two fixed dense random graphs
evidence.description: construct() -> two lists of cliques (vertex lists), one per instance from random_graph(n, p, seed) for (32,0.6,601) and (64,0.55,602) in the verifier (both with more than n^2/4 edges). Every listed set must be a clique with at least two vertices and every edge must lie in exactly one listed clique. Minimize the total number of cliques. The score totals clique partition sizes on two fixed dense graphs; it measures a partitioning method.

science-dense-triangle-free-four-chromat.rationale: The candidate returns the edge list of a graph on 16 vertices; the evaluator checks that it is triangle-free and, by exact backtracking, not 3-colourable, and scores the number of edges. Reviewed source family science_prize_f_four_chromatic_triangle_free, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Dense triangle-free graphs on 16 vertices with chromatic number at least four
evidence.description: construct() -> list of edges [u, v] of a simple triangle-free graph on vertices 0..15 that is not 3-colourable (exact backtracking). Maximize the number of edges. A valid graph with m edges shows f_4(16) > m; the published formula applies only to n >= 150.

science-diameter-two-edge-critical-graph.rationale: The candidate returns the edge list of a 16-vertex graph. The evaluator checks by breadth-first search that it has diameter two and that deleting any single edge increases the diameter, and scores the number of edges. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_610, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Dense graphs with every edge essential for diameter two
evidence.description: construct() -> simple undirected edges on vertices 0..15. The graph must have diameter exactly two. Deleting EACH individual edge must increase its diameter above two or disconnect it. Maximize edge count; the evaluator repeats exact all-pairs BFS for every edge deletion. Only sixteen vertices are searched; finite candidates provide lower constructions, not upper-bound proofs for every order. The star seed is an elementary complete bipartite example. No novelty or unresolved status of this small order is asserted.

science-disjoint-congruence-classes-128.rationale: The candidate constructs residue classes with distinct moduli between 2 and 128; the evaluator verifies pairwise disjointness with the exact gcd criterion, and the number of classes is maximized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_disjoint_congruences, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Many disjoint residue classes with distinct moduli
evidence.description: construct() -> a nonempty list of [residue,modulus] pairs with distinct moduli 2..maximum=128 and canonical residues 0<=r<m. Every two infinite residue classes must be disjoint; the verifier uses the exact gcd criterion. Maximize the number of classes. Choose pairwise disjoint infinite residue classes with distinct moduli between 2 and 128; maximize their number using the exact gcd/CRT criterion.

science-disjoint-residue-classes-moduli-.rationale: The candidate returns residue classes with distinct moduli in [20, 200]; the evaluator checks pairwise disjointness through gcd conditions and scores the exact sum of the reciprocals of the moduli. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_disjoint_classes, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Pairwise disjoint residue classes with distinct moduli in [20, 200] (largest reciprocal sum)
evidence.description: construct() -> classes [[m, r], ...] with distinct moduli 20 <= m <= 200 and 0 <= r < m, pairwise disjoint (r_1 != r_2 modulo gcd(m_1, m_2)). The score is the sum of 1/m (exact rational, reported as a float). Maximize. With moduli restricted to [20, 200] every valid construction bounds epsilon_19 from below.

science-distance-product-fixed-diameter-.rationale: The candidate returns 8 planar points; the evaluator rescales them to diameter 2 and scores the product of all pairwise distances relative to the regular octagon in floating point, which is maximized. Reviewed source family science_prize_g_distance_product, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Eight planar points maximizing the product of distances at fixed diameter
evidence.description: construct() -> 8 distinct points [x, y] (floats, |coordinate| < 10^6). The score is Delta/n^n, where Delta is the product over ordered pairs of distances after scaling the set to diameter 2; the regular octagon scores exactly 1. Maximize. Scores above 1 beat the regular octagon; the best published value for n = 8 is 1.250472 (Table 1 of the paper, conjectured optimal).

science-distinct-consecutive-prime-gaps-.rationale: The candidate names a starting prime and a length; the evaluator regenerates the consecutive primes below 10^8, checks that the gaps are pairwise distinct and scores the number of gaps. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_prime_gaps, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Longest string of pairwise distinct consecutive prime gaps below 10^8
evidence.description: construct() -> {'start': p, 'length': k} with p prime, 1 <= k <= 200, and the k + 1 consecutive primes beginning at p all at most 10^8. The k gaps between them must be pairwise distinct. Maximize k; the optimum below 10^8 is 21. Among primes below 10^8 the longest string has 21 distinct gaps, so the task recovers it.

science-distinct-divisor-counts-run-1e10.rationale: The candidate names a run of consecutive integers below 10^10; the evaluator factors each term exactly, checks that the divisor counts are pairwise distinct and scores the run length. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_divisor_run, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Longest run of consecutive integers with distinct divisor counts below 10^10
evidence.description: construct() -> {'start': s, 'length': k} with s >= 1, 1 <= k <= 40 and s + k - 1 <= 10^10. The divisor counts tau(s), ..., tau(s + k - 1) must be pairwise distinct (exact factorization). Maximize k; the optimum is 14. Runs ending below 10^10 have at most 14 terms, so the task recovers such a run.

science-distinct-modular-inverse-cover-1.rationale: For each residue modulo 101 the candidate gives distinct denominators in 1..10 whose modular inverses sum to that residue. The evaluator verifies every sum and scores the longest representation. Reviewed source family science_prize_d_modular_inverse_cover, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Short distinct-denominator inverse sums covering residues modulo 101
evidence.description: construct() -> 101 nonempty lists, row r containing distinct denominators in 1..10 whose modular inverses sum to r modulo 101. Every residue must be represented. Minimize the largest row length. Denominators may recur across different rows, but never within one row. The local p=101, denominator-bound-ten problem is a concrete finite covering certificate; it does not reproduce the all-prime, arbitrary-epsilon theorem.

science-distinct-multiple-worst-window.rationale: The candidate returns an interval start m. The evaluator computes by exact bipartite matching the shortest interval after m that contains distinct multiples of 1 to 12 and scores that length. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_580, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Worst interval starts for distinct-multiple matching
evidence.description: construct() -> Python integer m in 0..1000000. The evaluator computes f(12,m), the LEAST positive L such that (m,m+L] contains distinct b_1,...,b_12 with i dividing b_i. Maximize this independently computed L. Exact bipartite matching plus monotone binary search evaluates every proposal. The task fixes n=12 and bounds m by one million; it optimizes the exact finite f(n,m). It neither searches arbitrary integer sets as in JSP-000578 nor establishes asymptotic worst-case growth.

science-distinct-multiples-interval-50.rationale: The candidate assigns to each i = 1..50 a distinct multiple of i above 50; the evaluator checks divisibility and distinctness and scores the length of the interval that contains them. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_distinct_multiples, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Shortest interval above 50 containing distinct multiples of 1, ..., 50
evidence.description: construct() -> integers b_1, ..., b_50 with 50 < b_i <= 5000, i | b_i and all b_i distinct. The score is max(b) - 50 + 1, the least k with every b_i in the open interval (50, 50 + k). Minimize; the optimum is 77. For n = 50 the optimum is 77, so the task recovers an optimal matching.

science-distinct-subset-product-sets.rationale: The candidate returns a set of integers in 2..40. The evaluator enumerates all subset products, requires them to be distinct and scores the set size. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_653, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large sets with distinct subset products
evidence.description: construct() -> 1..18 distinct integers in 2..40. All 2^k subset products, including the empty product one, must be distinct. Exact arbitrary-precision products are enumerated. Maximize number of selected integers. The local instance restricts N=40 and certificate cardinality to 18 to bound exhaustive verification. It supplies finite constructions, not the paper’s asymptotic theorem; the optimum of this instance is 17 (OEIS A401472). Integer one is excluded because it collides with the empty product.

science-distinct-subset-sums-12.rationale: The candidate constructs 12 distinct positive integers; the evaluator verifies exactly that all 4096 subset sums are different, and the largest element is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_distinct_subset_sums, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Distinct subset sums with a small largest element
evidence.description: construct() -> exactly n=12 distinct positive Python integers <= maximum=1048576. Every subset, including the empty subset, must have a different sum. Minimize the largest integer. Exactly 12 positive integers with bounded largest entry; all 4096 subset sums checked. An improved feasible largest entry is only a finite upper bound.

science-distinct-three-unit-fractions-fo.rationale: The candidate supplies, for each n from 3 to 256, three distinct denominators with 1/x+1/y+1/z=4/n or no answer; the evaluator checks each identity by exact integer cross multiplication and scores the fraction of n solved. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_egyptian_four, area mathematics.

evidence.description: construct() -> 254 rows for n=3..256. Each row is None or three DISTINCT positive integer denominators x,y,z<=1000000000000 with 1/x+1/y+1/z=4/n. Maximize fraction solved. Equality is checked by cross multiplication and malformed claims invalidate the candidate. Construct distinct positive denominators for n=3..256, with denominator bound 10^12. The prize bank requires distinctness, which is stricter than the paper’s general solution definition; no universal proof or published computation is reproduced.

science-distinct-totient-runs-1e12.rationale: The candidate returns the start and length of a run of consecutive integers below 10^12; the evaluator computes Euler's totient of every term by exact factorization, requires the values to be pairwise distinct and scores the length. Reviewed source family science_prize_i_totient_run, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Long runs of consecutive integers with distinct totients (up to 10^12)
evidence.description: construct() -> {'start': s, 'length': k} with s >= 1, 1 <= k <= 200 and s + k - 1 <= 10^12. The values phi(s), ..., phi(s + k - 1) must be pairwise distinct (exact factorization). Maximize k. The length cap 200 is attained: runs of 200 consecutive integers with distinct totients occur below 1.2*10^6 and a sieve finds one in seconds. So 200 is the maximum score, the bound 10^12 plays no role, and the task is a capped search exercise rather than evidence on the conjecture.

science-double-cover-primes-to-1000.rationale: The candidate chooses one residue class for each prime up to 1000; the evaluator counts exactly how long an initial interval 1..L is covered at least twice. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_double_cover, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Covering an initial interval twice with one residue class per prime up to 1000
evidence.description: construct() -> 168 residues, one for each prime p <= 1000 in increasing order, with 0 <= r_p < p. The score is the largest L such that every integer 1..L satisfies at least two of the congruences x = r_p (mod p) (exact count, capped at 10^5). Maximize; L >= 1000 would realize the property asked in Erdős Problem #689 at n = 1000. Scores are doubly covered lengths for n = 1000; reaching 1000 would exhibit the property at this size.

science-earth-arctic-sea-ice-drift.rationale: The candidate fits a drift model on 2000-2014 buoy tracks and geostrophic winds and forecasts each buoy's daily ice velocity for 2015-2024 one day at a time. The evaluator scores the root-mean-square vector error against the observed buoy displacements. Reviewed source family earth_research_sea_ice_drift, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: daily Arctic sea-ice drift from geostrophic winds
evidence.description: Learn how Arctic sea ice drifts in response to the wind from 2000-2014 drifting-buoy tracks and reanalysis sea-level pressure, then predict the daily velocity of every buoy north of 70 N for each day of 2015-2024 from that day's geostrophic wind and the past buoy record. The score is the root-mean-square vector error of the predicted velocities.

science-earth-camels-runoff.rationale: The source names a climate, hydrological, geophysical or environmental inference/forecasting target; its data may be simulated or measured as declared in the package. Reviewed source family science_earth_e01, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth and environment: Measured rainfall–runoff transfer across catchments
evidence.description: Calibrate a causal, water-conserving snow/soil runoff model on measured CAMELS catchments and predict discharge in wholly unseen basins and a subsequent year.

science-earth-climatebench-emissions-res.rationale: The source names a climate, hydrological, geophysical or environmental inference/forecasting target; its data may be simulated or measured as declared in the package. Reviewed source family science_earth_e05, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth and environment: ClimateBench emissions-to-climate response
evidence.description: Learn a compact emissions-response emulator from complete training scenarios and predict source climate anomalies for the entirely withheldSSP245 scenario.

science-earth-earthquake-b-value-complet.rationale: The candidate estimates the Gutenberg-Richter b-value and the completeness magnitude of 600 synthetic, incompletely detected earthquake catalogues. The evaluator scores the mean absolute b-value error against the generating values. Reviewed source family earth_research_b_value, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: Gutenberg-Richter b-value from incomplete earthquake catalogues
evidence.description: Estimate the Gutenberg-Richter b-value and the magnitude of completeness of 600 synthetic earthquake catalogues whose small events are missed according to a realistic detection probability. The score is the mean absolute error of the estimated b-values against the generating values.

science-earth-enso-nino34-forecast.rationale: The candidate fits a statistical model on 1950-1999 sea-surface temperatures and forecasts the monthly Nino 3.4 index 1-12 months ahead from every 2000-2024 origin, seeing data only up to the origin. The evaluator scores the mean over leads of the root-mean-square error. Reviewed source family earth_research_enso, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: El Nino-Southern Oscillation forecasts of the Nino 3.4 index
evidence.description: Fit a statistical ENSO forecast model on 1950-1999 ERSSTv5 sea-surface temperatures and, for every month from 2000 to 2024, forecast the monthly Nino 3.4 index for the next 12 months using only data up to that month. The score is the mean root-mean-square error over the 12 lead times.

science-earth-fluxnet-ecosystem-flux.rationale: The source names a climate, hydrological, geophysical or environmental inference/forecasting target; its data may be simulated or measured as declared in the package. Reviewed source family science_earth_e02, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth and environment: Measured ecosystem carbon-flux reconstruction
evidence.description: Predict half-hourly net ecosystem carbon exchange from meteorology and ecosystem metadata, scoring quality-controlled measured targets rather than gap-filled products.

science-earth-global-aftershock-forecast.rationale: The candidate fits an aftershock model on 1990-2014 sequences and issues binned probabilities for the number of magnitude 5+ aftershocks after large shallow earthquakes of 2015-2024, using only earlier events. The evaluator scores the mean log probability of the observed count bins. Reviewed source family earth_research_aftershock_counts, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: probabilistic aftershock forecasts after large earthquakes worldwide
evidence.description: Fit an aftershock forecasting model on 1990-2014 sequences from the global ComCat catalogue and, for every large shallow earthquake of 2015-2024, forecast the probability distribution of the number of magnitude 5 or larger aftershocks in the week after day 1 and the month after day 7, using only events before each forecast. The score is the mean logarithmic score of the observed counts.

science-earth-global-temperature-emulati.rationale: The candidate fits a model of annual global mean temperature on 1850-1979 observations with radiative-forcing and ENSO inputs and predicts the 1980-2024 anomalies. The evaluator scores the root-mean-square error against the withheld HadCRUT5 values. Reviewed source family earth_research_gmst_emulation, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: predicting recent global warming from forcing and early observations
evidence.description: Fit a model of annual global mean surface temperature on the 1850-1979 HadCRUT5 record, given radiative forcing histories and an ENSO index for 1750-2024, and predict the 1980-2024 anomalies without seeing any later temperature. The score is the root-mean-square error of the predicted anomalies.

science-earth-great-lakes-wave-hindcast.rationale: The candidate learns from 2009-2018 buoy records and hindcasts hourly significant wave height at seven Great Lakes buoys for 2019-2024 from their meteorology. The evaluator scores the root-mean-square error against the withheld wave observations. Reviewed source family earth_research_great_lakes_waves, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: Great Lakes wave height from buoy meteorology
evidence.description: Learn how wind and other meteorology at seven NOAA buoys on Lakes Superior, Michigan, Huron and Erie generate waves from 2009-2018 records, then hindcast the hourly significant wave height for 2019-2024 from the buoys' meteorology alone. The score is the root-mean-square error of the hindcast wave heights.

science-earth-groundwater-uncertainty.rationale: The source names a climate, hydrological, geophysical or environmental inference/forecasting target; its data may be simulated or measured as declared in the package. Reviewed source family science_earth_groundwater, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.description: Groundwater predictive uncertainty with an explicit candidate interface, physical units, independent evaluator and source-traceable observations or numerical model.

science-earth-hurricane-intensity-foreca.rationale: The candidate fits a statistical model on the 1950-2014 Atlantic best track and forecasts maximum sustained wind 12-120 h ahead for held-out 2015-2024 storms from each storm's history. The evaluator scores the mean absolute error over seven lead times against the best track. Reviewed source family earth_research_tc_intensity, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: Atlantic hurricane intensity forecasting from the best track
evidence.description: Fit a statistical tropical-cyclone intensity model on the 1950-2014 Atlantic best track and forecast the 12-120 h maximum sustained wind for every advisory-time record of the held-out 2015-2024 storms. The score is the mean absolute intensity error over seven lead times.

science-earth-hurricane-track-forecast.rationale: The candidate fits a statistical model on the 1950-2014 Atlantic best track and forecasts storm-centre positions 12-120 h ahead for held-out 2015-2024 storms from each storm's history. The evaluator scores the mean great-circle distance over seven lead times against the best track. Reviewed source family earth_research_tc_track, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: Atlantic hurricane track forecasting from the best track
evidence.description: Fit a statistical tropical-cyclone track model on the 1950-2014 Atlantic best track and forecast 12-120 h centre positions for every advisory-time record of the held-out 2015-2024 storms. The score is the mean great-circle track error over seven lead times.

science-earth-hurricane-wind-radii-forec.rationale: The candidate fits a storm-size model on 2004-2014 best-track wind radii and forecasts the 34-kt radii in four quadrants 12-72 h ahead for 2015-2024 storms, given the verifying track and intensity. The evaluator scores the mean absolute radius error. Reviewed source family earth_research_tc_wind_radii, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: Atlantic hurricane wind-radii (storm size) forecasting
evidence.description: Fit a model of tropical-cyclone size on the 2004-2014 Atlantic best track and forecast the radius of 34-kt winds in four quadrants 12-72 h ahead for every analysed time of the 2015-2024 storms, given the storm's history and its best-track track and intensity at the verifying times. The score is the mean absolute radius error.

science-earth-irrigation-policies.rationale: The candidate chooses sequential irrigation actions from past weather and current soil state under water limits; scoring uses a declared crop simulator. Reviewed source family science_earth_irrigation, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.description: Water-efficient irrigation policies with an explicit candidate interface, physical units, independent evaluator and source-traceable observations or numerical model.

science-earth-mauna-loa-co2-forecast.rationale: The candidate fits a forecast model on the Mauna Loa monthly CO2 record up to 1999 with an ENSO index and forecasts the next 12 monthly means from every 2000-2024 origin. The evaluator scores the mean over leads of the root-mean-square error. Reviewed source family earth_research_co2_forecast, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: monthly Mauna Loa CO2 forecasts
evidence.description: Fit a forecast model of atmospheric CO2 on the Mauna Loa monthly record up to 1999, together with an ENSO index, and for every month from 2000 to 2024 forecast the next 12 monthly means using only data up to that month. The score is the mean root-mean-square error over the 12 lead times.

science-earth-methane-emission-inversion.rationale: The source names a climate, hydrological, geophysical or environmental inference/forecasting target; its data may be simulated or measured as declared in the package. Reviewed source family science_earth_methane, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.description: Methane emission inversion with an explicit candidate interface, physical units, independent evaluator and source-traceable observations or numerical model.

science-earth-oceanbench-satellite-ssh.rationale: The source names a climate, hydrological, geophysical or environmental inference/forecasting target; its data may be simulated or measured as declared in the package. Reviewed source family science_earth_e06, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth and environment: Independent-track ocean surface-height reconstruction
evidence.description: Reconstruct measured sea-surface-height anomalies from irregular satellite observations and evaluate a fully withheld satellite system.

science-earth-openfwi-seismic-inversion.rationale: The source names a climate, hydrological, geophysical or environmental inference/forecasting target; its data may be simulated or measured as declared in the package. Reviewed source family science_earth_e04, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth and environment: OpenFWI subsurface seismic inversion
evidence.description: Reconstruct a positive subsurface velocity field from simulated seismic traces, independently checking velocity structure and a pinned source-matching wave forward model.

science-earth-river-nitrate-loads.rationale: The candidate estimates daily nitrate concentrations in eight rivers from sparse samples and daily discharge. The evaluator scores the mean absolute relative error of monthly loads against loads computed from withheld continuous sensor records. Reviewed source family earth_research_river_nitrate, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: river nitrate loads from sparse samples
evidence.description: Estimate daily nitrate concentrations in eight U.S. rivers from about 16 samples per year and continuous daily discharge, as in routine water-quality monitoring. The score is the error of the resulting monthly nitrate loads against loads computed from continuous in-situ nitrate sensors, which the candidate never sees.

science-earth-seasonal-sea-ice.rationale: The source names a climate, hydrological, geophysical or environmental inference/forecasting target; its data may be simulated or measured as declared in the package. Reviewed source family science_earth_ice, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: Seasonal Arctic sea-ice probabilities
evidence.description: Seasonal Arctic sea-ice probabilities with an explicit candidate interface, physical units, independent evaluator and source-traceable observations or numerical model.

science-earth-snow-accumulation-melt.rationale: The candidate advances snow stores and fluxes through time while maintaining the specified water-balance constraints, evaluated against source snow observations. Reviewed source family science_earth_snow, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: Snow accumulation and melt across sites
evidence.description: Snow accumulation and melt across sites with an explicit candidate interface, physical units, independent evaluator and source-traceable observations or numerical model.

science-earth-snow-depth-to-swe.rationale: The candidate learns a depth-to-water-equivalent conversion from 114 SNOTEL stations and predicts snow water equivalent from snow depth at 48 held-out stations. The evaluator scores the root-mean-square error on the held-out stations' snow days. Reviewed source family earth_research_snow_depth_to_swe, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: snow water equivalent from snow depth at unseen stations
evidence.description: Convert daily snow depth to snow water equivalent at 48 held-out SNOTEL stations across the western United States and Alaska, after learning from 114 other stations with both measurements over water years 2006-2025. The score is the root-mean-square error of snow water equivalent on the held-out stations' snow days.

science-earth-socal-earthquake-forecast.rationale: The candidate fits an earthquake occurrence model on the 1981-2015 southern California catalogue and forecasts expected daily counts per 0.1-degree cell for 2016-2024 from earlier events only. The evaluator scores the Poisson information gain per earthquake over a smoothed-seismicity reference. Reviewed source family earth_research_socal_quakes, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: one-day earthquake forecasts for southern California
evidence.description: Fit an earthquake occurrence model on the 1981-2015 southern California ComCat catalogue and, for every day of 2016-2024, forecast the expected number of magnitude 3.45 or larger earthquakes in each 0.1-degree cell using only events before that day. The score is the information gain per earthquake of the Poisson likelihood over a time-independent smoothed-seismicity reference.

science-earth-solar-irradiance-separatio.rationale: The candidate learns a separation model from four SURFRAD stations and estimates 1-minute diffuse irradiance at three other stations from global irradiance, solar geometry and meteorology. The evaluator scores the root-mean-square error against the withheld diffuse measurements. Reviewed source family earth_research_solar_separation, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: diffuse solar irradiance from global irradiance at unseen stations
evidence.description: Learn a separation model from 1-minute measurements of global, direct and diffuse solar irradiance at four NOAA SURFRAD stations and estimate the diffuse irradiance at three other stations from their global irradiance, solar geometry and meteorology on 48 days of 2022-2023. The score is the root-mean-square error of the estimated diffuse irradiance.

science-earth-species-distribution-model.rationale: The candidate fits species distribution models from presence-only records, background points and environmental covariates and scores independent survey sites. The evaluator computes the mean ROC AUC over 226 species against withheld presence-absence outcomes. Reviewed source family earth_research_species_distribution, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: species distribution models from presence-only records
evidence.description: Fit species distribution models for 226 anonymised species in six regions from presence-only records, background points and environmental covariates, and score sites of independent presence-absence surveys whose outcomes are withheld. The score is the mean area under the ROC curve over species.

science-earth-temperature-homogenization.rationale: The candidate removes non-climatic breaks, drifts and outliers from synthetic networks of monthly station temperature series. The evaluator scores the centred root-mean-square difference between the homogenised and the true annual means. Reviewed source family earth_research_homogenization, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: homogenisation of monthly temperature networks
evidence.description: Remove non-climatic breaks, drifts and outliers from 40 synthetic networks of ten correlated 100-year monthly temperature records, as climate-data centres do before estimating trends. The score is the mean centred root-mean-square difference between the homogenised and the true annual means, which the generator knows exactly.

science-earth-two-stream-radiative-trans.rationale: The candidate supplies two-stream closure coefficients as functions of single-scattering albedo, asymmetry parameter and sun angle. The evaluator solves the two-stream equations for 12000 layers and scores the reflectance and transmittance error against a 96-stream discrete-ordinate solution. Reviewed source family earth_research_two_stream, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: two-stream closures for solar radiative transfer
evidence.description: Design the coefficients of a two-stream approximation for sunlight in a scattering and absorbing atmospheric layer as functions of single-scattering albedo, asymmetry parameter and solar zenith angle. The evaluator solves the two-stream equations for 12000 layers and scores the mean reflectance and transmittance error against an accurate 96-stream discrete-ordinate solution.

science-earth-weatherbench-calibration.rationale: The source names a climate, hydrological, geophysical or environmental inference/forecasting target; its data may be simulated or measured as declared in the package. Reviewed source family science_earth_e03, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth and environment: WeatherBench probabilistic forecast calibration
evidence.description: Calibrate fixed operational ensemble forecasts using prior-year history and evaluate their predictive distributions against independently aligned future-year reanalysis.

science-earth-wildfire-spread-law.rationale: The source names a climate, hydrological, geophysical or environmental inference/forecasting target; its data may be simulated or measured as declared in the package. Reviewed source family science_earth_fire, area earth_and_environment.

evidence.task_name: Earth science: Measured wildfire spread laws
evidence.description: Measured wildfire spread laws with an explicit candidate interface, physical units, independent evaluator and source-traceable observations or numerical model.

science-economics-consumption-saving.rationale: The candidate defines a consumption-saving or exercise policy under a fixed economic model and information boundary; no real investment return is established. Reviewed source family science_economics_consumption, area finance.

evidence.description: Consumption-saving policy accuracy with an explicit candidate API, independently recomputed objective and fixed model/data assumptions.

science-economics-finite-auction-design.rationale: The candidate constructs a finite allocation/payment mechanism under explicit feasibility, individual-rationality and incentive constraints. Reviewed source family science_economics_auctions, area finance.

evidence.description: Incentive-compatible finite auction design with an explicit candidate API, independently recomputed objective and fixed model/data assumptions.

science-economics-fredmd-industrial-prod.rationale: The candidate forecasts one macroeconomic series 1, 6 and 12 months ahead from the FRED-MD panel available at each monthly origin; the evaluator recomputes the targets and scores the forecast error relative to an autoregressive benchmark. Reviewed source family science_economics_fredmd_forecast, area finance.

evidence.task_name: Economics: Forecasting US industrial production with FRED-MD
evidence.description: Forecast annualized US industrial-production growth 1, 6 and 12 months ahead from the 126-series FRED-MD panel available at each month-end origin from 1990 to 2023. The evaluator recomputes the targets and scores the root-mean-square error relative to a direct autoregressive benchmark with BIC lag selection.

science-economics-fredmd-inflation-forec.rationale: The candidate forecasts one macroeconomic series 1, 6 and 12 months ahead from the FRED-MD panel available at each monthly origin; the evaluator recomputes the targets and scores the forecast error relative to an autoregressive benchmark. Reviewed source family science_economics_fredmd_forecast, area finance.

evidence.task_name: Economics: Forecasting US CPI inflation with FRED-MD
evidence.description: Forecast annualized US CPI inflation 1, 6 and 12 months ahead from the 126-series FRED-MD panel available at each month-end origin from 1990 to 2023. The evaluator recomputes the targets and scores the root-mean-square error relative to a direct autoregressive benchmark with BIC lag selection.

science-economics-fredmd-unemployment-fo.rationale: The candidate forecasts one macroeconomic series 1, 6 and 12 months ahead from the FRED-MD panel available at each monthly origin; the evaluator recomputes the targets and scores the forecast error relative to an autoregressive benchmark. Reviewed source family science_economics_fredmd_forecast, area finance.

evidence.task_name: Economics: Forecasting US unemployment with FRED-MD
evidence.description: Forecast the change in the US unemployment rate 1, 6 and 12 months ahead from the 126-series FRED-MD panel available at each month-end origin from 1990 to 2023. The evaluator recomputes the targets and scores the root-mean-square error relative to a direct autoregressive benchmark with BIC lag selection.

science-economics-kidney-exchange.rationale: The candidate selects vertex-disjoint two- and three-way exchange cycles in eight PrefLib kidney pools; the evaluator verifies every donor-patient edge and the disjointness of the cycles and scores total transplants divided by the stored optimum. Reviewed source family science_economics_kidney_exchange, area finance.

evidence.task_name: Economics: Kidney exchange clearing with two- and three-way cycles
evidence.description: Choose vertex-disjoint two- and three-way exchange cycles in eight public kidney-exchange pools of 256 and 512 incompatible patient-donor pairs to maximize the number of transplants. The evaluator verifies every donor-patient compatibility on the chosen cycles and compares the transplant count with the proven optimum.

science-economics-macroeconomic-transiti.rationale: The candidate solves a macroeconomic equilibrium transition path, evaluated by independently recomputed market residuals under fixed model assumptions. Reviewed source family science_economics_macro, area finance.

evidence.description: Heterogeneous-agent macroeconomic transitions with an explicit candidate API, independently recomputed objective and fixed model/data assumptions.

science-economics-maximum-nash-welfare.rationale: The candidate assigns indivisible goods to agents with additive integer valuations on eight fixed synthetic instances; the evaluator recomputes each allocation's Nash welfare (geometric mean utility) and scores its mean ratio to the stored integer-programming optimum. Reviewed source family science_economics_nash_welfare, area finance.

evidence.task_name: Economics: Maximum Nash welfare allocation of indivisible goods
evidence.description: Allocate indivisible goods among agents with additive Spliddit-style valuations to maximize Nash welfare, the geometric mean of the agents' utilities. The evaluator recomputes each allocation's Nash welfare and compares it with the proven optimum on eight fixed instances with 4 to 15 agents.

science-economics-optimal-stopping.rationale: The candidate defines a consumption-saving or exercise policy under a fixed economic model and information boundary; no real investment return is established. Reviewed source family science_economics_stopping, area finance.

evidence.description: Bermudan exercise-policy research with an explicit candidate API, independently recomputed objective and fixed model/data assumptions.

science-economics-school-choice-tie-brea.rationale: The candidate assigns students to schools with coarse priorities on six synthetic markets; the evaluator checks lists, capacities and every blocking pair for weak stability and scores the share of the total-rank reduction from deferred acceptance with single tie-breaking to the stored optimum. Reviewed source family science_economics_school_choice, area finance.

evidence.task_name: Economics: Efficient school choice under coarse priorities
evidence.description: Assign students to schools when school priorities have many ties, improving on deferred acceptance with a single tie-breaking lottery (DA-STB) while keeping the matching weakly stable. The evaluator checks every student-school pair for blocking and scores the share of the possible reduction in total preference rank achieved on six synthetic markets.

science-economics-structural-demand-esti.rationale: The candidate estimates a structural demand parameter from product data using the declared moment objective and independent numerical re-evaluation. Reviewed source family science_economics_demand, area finance.

evidence.description: Structural differentiated-product demand estimation with an explicit candidate API, independently recomputed objective and fixed model/data assumptions.

science-edge-disjoint-monochromatic-tria.rationale: The candidate returns a red/blue colouring of the 55 edges of K11; the evaluator computes the maximum number of edge-disjoint monochromatic triangles exactly by branch and bound, and fewer is better. Reviewed source family science_prize_e_monochromatic_triangle_packing, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Two-colourings of K11 with few edge-disjoint monochromatic triangles
evidence.description: construct() -> {'n': 11, 'colors': [...]}: colour 0 or 1 for each of the 55 pairs (i,j), i<j, in lexicographic order. The score is the maximum number of edge-disjoint monochromatic triangles, computed exactly per colour by branch and bound. Minimize; the known optimum is 6. Any colouring gives an upper bound on the minimum; the tabulated value for n = 11 is 6.

science-equal-area-triangle-multiplicity.rationale: The candidate places 30 integer points in a bounded square. The evaluator computes the area of every triangle and scores the largest number of triangles sharing one nonzero area. Reviewed source family science_prize_d_equal_area, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Many equal-area triangles from 30 planar points
evidence.description: construct() -> exactly 30 distinct integer coordinate pairs in [-30,30]^2. Compute the absolute determinant for every triple, exclude zero-area triples, and maximize the largest multiplicity of a single positive doubled area. The local bounded integer configurations give lower constructions for positive-area multiplicity; they do not reproduce the paper's asymptotic upper-bound proof.

science-equal-degree-three-path-avoidanc.rationale: The candidate returns the edge list of a 15-vertex graph. The evaluator checks that no three-edge path joins two vertices of equal degree and scores the number of edges. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_673, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Dense odd-order graphs avoiding equal-degree path endpoints
evidence.description: construct() -> simple undirected edges on vertices 0..14. Reject if any simple three-edge path has endpoints of equal degree in the FULL candidate graph. Extra chords are allowed: paths need not be induced. Maximize edge count. The local order fifteen lies outside the cited n>=600 theorem. Every length-three path is checked directly; no use of the asymptotic edge threshold to reject valid candidates is made.

science-equal-divisor-sum-ratio-approxim.rationale: The candidate returns two integers up to ten million with equal sum of divisors. The evaluator recomputes both divisor sums and scores the exact distance of their ratio from 3/2. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_679, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Approximate a ratio inside a divisor-sum fiber
evidence.description: construct() -> [a,b], positive Python integers <=10000000. Require sigma(a)=sigma(b), where sigma includes ALL positive divisors. Minimize |a/b-3/2|. Factorization and rational error are exact; the score is the binary64 serialization of that rational, with its exact numerator/denominator reported. Only the target 3/2 and inputs bounded by ten million are evaluated. A smaller exact rational error is a finite approximation, not a density proof for all positive real targets. Tiny error differences can round to the same floating score.

science-erdos-gyarfas-five-colours-k16.rationale: The candidate returns an edge colouring of K16; the evaluator checks that every four vertices span at least five colours and counts the colours used, fewer being better. Reviewed source family science_prize_e_four_clique_colours, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Edge-colourings of K16 in which every K4 sees five colours
evidence.description: construct() -> 120 integer colours in 0..119 for the pairs (i,j), 0<=i<j<16, in lexicographic order. Every set of four vertices must span edges of at least five distinct colours. Minimize the number of colours used. A valid colouring certifies f(16) <= colours used. The known bounds give 14 <= f(16) <= 15; no exact value for n = 16 is documented.

science-erdos-rogers-k4-free-18.rationale: The candidate returns the edge list of a K4-free graph on 18 vertices; the evaluator computes exactly the largest vertex set inducing a triangle-free subgraph, and smaller is better. Reviewed source family science_prize_f_erdos_rogers, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: K4-free graphs on 18 vertices with small triangle-free induced subgraphs (Erdős-Rogers)
evidence.description: construct() -> list of edges [u, v] of a simple K4-free graph on vertices 0..17. The score is the largest number of vertices inducing a triangle-free subgraph (exact branch and bound). Minimize. A K4-free graph whose triangle-free induced subgraphs have at most s vertices certifies f(18) <= s; no exact value for n = 18 is documented.

science-few-monochromatic-four-progressi.rationale: The candidate returns a two-colouring of the integers 1..256; the evaluator counts every monochromatic four-term arithmetic progression exactly, and fewer is better. Reviewed source family science_prize_e_monochromatic_progressions, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Two-colourings of [1,256] with few monochromatic four-term progressions
evidence.description: construct() -> 256 colours in {0,1} for the integers 1..256. Minimize the exact number of monochromatic 4-term arithmetic progressions a, a+d, a+2d, a+3d with d >= 1 inside 1..256. The finite count for n = 256 and k = 4 upper-bounds the minimum for this n; no exact finite value is documented.

science-finance-arbitrage-free-svi-surfa.rationale: The candidate fits raw SVI parameters to each of eight maturities of a DAX implied-volatility surface; the evaluator checks butterfly and calendar-spread arbitrage conditions on a dense moneyness grid and scores the root-mean-square implied-volatility error over the 104 quotes. Reviewed source family science_finance_svi_surface, area finance.

evidence.task_name: Finance: Arbitrage-free SVI implied-volatility surface for DAX options
evidence.description: Fit a raw SVI smile to each of the eight maturities of a real DAX option implied-volatility surface (2002-07-05, 104 quotes) without static arbitrage. The evaluator checks butterfly and calendar-spread arbitrage on a dense moneyness grid and scores the root-mean-square implied-volatility error in volatility points.

science-finance-cardinality-constrained-.rationale: The candidate builds, for five OR-Library markets, portfolios of exactly ten assets with holding bounds at 51 fixed target returns; the evaluator checks every constraint and scores the mean percentage deviation from the published unconstrained efficient frontier. Reviewed source family science_finance_cardinality_frontier, area finance.

evidence.description: Build mean-variance portfolios of exactly ten assets, each held between 1% and 100%, at 51 fixed target returns for five OR-Library stock markets with 31 to 225 assets. The evaluator checks every constraint and scores Chang et al.'s mean percentage deviation from the published unconstrained efficient frontier.

science-finance-covariance-minimum-varia.rationale: The candidate estimates the covariance matrix of 49 industry portfolios from the previous 126 daily returns; the evaluator forms the global minimum-variance portfolio from each estimate every 21 days and scores the annualized standard deviation of its out-of-sample returns. Reviewed source family science_finance_covariance_gmv, area finance.

evidence.task_name: Finance: Covariance estimation for minimum-variance portfolios
evidence.description: Estimate the covariance matrix of 49 US industry portfolios from the previous 126 daily returns so that the implied global minimum-variance portfolio has the lowest realized out-of-sample volatility. The evaluator forms the portfolio from each estimate every 21 trading days from 1971 to 2025 and scores the annualized standard deviation of its daily returns.

science-finance-equity-premium-predictio.rationale: The candidate forecasts next month's log equity premium from the Welch-Goyal predictor data observed up to each origin; the evaluator recomputes the out-of-sample R-squared against the prevailing historical mean over the monthly targets from 1965 to 2025. Reviewed source family science_finance_equity_premium, area finance.

evidence.description: Forecast next month's US equity premium (the log S&P 500 return over the T-bill rate) from the Welch-Goyal predictors observed up to the forecast origin. The evaluator recomputes the out-of-sample R^2 against the prevailing historical mean over 732 monthly forecasts from 1965-01 to 2025-12.

science-finance-index-tracking.rationale: The candidate chooses and periodically rebalances a portfolio of at most ten constituents for five OR-Library index markets using prices up to each decision week; the evaluator recomputes portfolio values net of trading costs and scores the out-of-sample tracking error. Reviewed source family science_finance_index_tracking, area finance.

evidence.task_name: Finance: Index tracking with few stocks and transaction costs (OR-Library)
evidence.description: Track five stock indices (Hang Seng, DAX 100, FTSE 100, S&P 100 and Nikkei 225) with buy-and-hold positions in at most ten constituents, formed from the first 145 weeks of prices and optionally rebalanced every 13 weeks at a 1% cost. The evaluator recomputes the portfolio values and scores the out-of-sample tracking error over the last 145 weeks.

science-finance-market-making.rationale: The candidate sets bid and ask depths from time and inventory in a discrete Avellaneda-Stoikov simulator; the evaluator simulates fills on fixed random numbers in three regimes and scores risk-adjusted profit relative to the dynamic-programming policy of the same model. Reviewed source family science_finance_market_making, area finance.

evidence.task_name: Finance: Optimal market making with inventory risk
evidence.description: Set bid and ask quotes around the mid price in the Avellaneda-Stoikov limit-order-book model to earn the spread while controlling inventory risk, in three simulated market regimes. The evaluator simulates fills on fixed random numbers and scores the risk-adjusted profit relative to the exact optimal quoting policy.

science-finance-optimal-execution.rationale: The candidate returns a sell schedule for twelve fixed instances of the Almgren-Chriss market-impact model; the evaluator recomputes the mean-variance cost of each schedule exactly and scores its percentage excess over the closed-form or convex-solver optimum. Reviewed source family science_finance_optimal_execution, area finance.

evidence.task_name: Finance: Optimal execution under Almgren-Chriss market impact
evidence.description: Schedule the sale of a large block of shares over a fixed horizon to minimize expected trading cost plus a variance penalty in the Almgren-Chriss market-impact model, including power-law impact and an intraday liquidity profile. The evaluator recomputes each schedule's cost-risk objective exactly and compares it with the known optimum on 12 fixed instances.

science-finance-portfolio-choice-ff20.rationale: The candidate chooses each month's portfolio weights from the preceding window of excess returns; the evaluator applies them to the next month, charges proportional trading costs and scores the Sharpe ratio of the net out-of-sample returns. Reviewed source family science_finance_portfolio_choice_dgu, area finance.

evidence.task_name: Finance: Out-of-sample portfolio choice against 1/N (20 size and value portfolios and the market)
evidence.description: Choose each month's portfolio of 20 size and book-to-market portfolios and the market using only the previous 120 months of returns. The evaluator recomputes the Sharpe ratio of the next-month returns net of 50 bp trading costs over 1973-07 to 2025-09 and compares it with the 1/N rule.

science-finance-portfolio-choice-industr.rationale: The candidate chooses each month's portfolio weights from the preceding window of excess returns; the evaluator applies them to the next month, charges proportional trading costs and scores the Sharpe ratio of the net out-of-sample returns. Reviewed source family science_finance_portfolio_choice_dgu, area finance.

evidence.task_name: Finance: Out-of-sample portfolio choice against 1/N (ten industries and the market)
evidence.description: Choose each month's portfolio of ten US industry portfolios and the market using only the previous 120 months of returns. The evaluator recomputes the Sharpe ratio of the next-month returns net of 50 bp trading costs over 1973-07 to 2025-09 and compares it with the 1/N rule.

science-finance-portfolio-choice-industr.rationale: The candidate chooses each month's weights over 49 industry portfolios from the previous 120 months of excess returns; the evaluator applies them to the next month, charges proportional trading costs and scores the monthly Sharpe ratio of the net out-of-sample returns. Reviewed source family science_finance_portfolio_choice, area finance.

evidence.task_name: Finance: Out-of-sample portfolio choice against 1/N (49 industries)
evidence.description: Choose each month's portfolio of 49 US industry portfolios using only the previous 120 months of returns, a setting where estimation error is severe. The evaluator recomputes the Sharpe ratio of the next-month returns net of 50 bp trading costs over 1979-07 to 2025-09 and compares it with the 1/N rule.

science-finance-volatility-forecasting.rationale: The candidate forecasts the next day's return variance of the US market and 49 industry portfolios, updating day by day from 2000 to 2025; the evaluator reveals each day's returns only after the forecast and scores the mean QLIKE loss against squared returns. Reviewed source family science_finance_volatility_forecast, area finance.

evidence.task_name: Finance: Daily volatility forecasting for US equity portfolios
evidence.description: Forecast the next day's return variance of the US stock market and 49 industry portfolios, updating the forecasts day by day from 2000 to 2025 after a training period ending in 1999. The evaluator reveals each day's returns only after the forecasts are made and scores the QLIKE loss against squared returns.

science-finance-yield-curve-forecasting.rationale: The candidate forecasts US Treasury zero-coupon yields at maturities of 1 to 10 years, 1, 6 and 12 months ahead, from the curves observed up to each origin; the evaluator scores the root-mean-square error relative to the no-change forecast. Reviewed source family science_finance_yield_curve_forecast, area finance.

evidence.task_name: Finance: Forecasting the US Treasury yield curve

science-mutually-orthogonal-latin-square.rationale: The candidate returns a list of 10-by-10 Latin squares. The evaluator checks each square and the orthogonality of every pair and scores the number of squares. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_592, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order ten
evidence.description: construct() -> a nonempty list of 10-by-10 arrays with Python integer symbols 0..9. Every row and column must contain each symbol exactly once. For every two arrays, their 100 ordered symbol pairs must be distinct. Maximize the number of pairwise orthogonal arrays. Only order ten is evaluated. The cyclic single-square baseline does not implement Wilson’s recursive constructions. No current best-known N(10), global optimality or novel family is asserted.

science-narrow-factorization-of-30-facto.rationale: The candidate returns strictly increasing integers whose product is 30!; the evaluator checks the product exactly and scores the difference between the largest and the smallest factor.
