Reviewed source family science_prize_h_factorial_span, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Narrowest factorization of 30! into increasing factors
evidence.description: construct() -> strictly increasing positive integers a_1 < ... < a_t with 2 <= t <= 30 and product exactly 30!. Minimize a_t - a_1; the optimum is 27. For n = 30 the optimum span is 27, so the task recovers an optimal factorization.

science-no-element-divides-two-others-44.rationale: The candidate returns a subset of {1..44}; the evaluator checks that no element divides two others and scores the size. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_divides_two, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Subsets of {1, ..., 44} in which no element divides two others
evidence.description: construct() -> distinct integers in 1..44 such that no element divides two other elements. Maximize the size; the optimum is 30. For n = 44 the maximum is 30, so the task recovers an extremal set.

science-no-four-collinear-general-positi.rationale: The candidate returns 20 integer points with no four on a line; the evaluator computes the largest subset with no three collinear by exact branch and bound and scores its size, which is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_g_general_position, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Twenty points with no four collinear and small general-position subsets
evidence.description: construct() -> exactly 20 distinct integer points [x, y] with |x|, |y| <= 100 and no four collinear. The score is the largest subset with no three collinear (exact branch and bound). Minimize. A valid configuration with score s certifies g(20) <= s; no exact value for n = 20 is documented.

science-no-square-subset-sums-134.rationale: The candidate returns a subset of {1..134}; the evaluator computes all subset sums exactly, rejects the set if any of them is a perfect square and scores the size. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_square_subset_sums, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large subsets of {1, ..., 134} with no subset sum a perfect square
evidence.description: construct() -> distinct integers in 1..134 such that no nonempty subset sums to a perfect square (exact subset-sum bitset). Maximize the size; the optimum is 13. For N = 134 the maximum is 13, so the task recovers an extremal set.

science-nonaveraging-integer-set-512.rationale: The candidate constructs at most 48 distinct integers in [1,512] in which no element is the mean of two or more other elements; the evaluator checks every subset size with an exact subset-sum computation, and the size of the set is maximized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_nonaveraging, area mathematics.

evidence.description: construct() -> 1..maximum=48 distinct positive integers <=n=512. No element may be the exact arithmetic mean of any subset of at least two OTHER elements. The verifier checks every possible subset cardinality by integer bitsets. Maximize cardinality. At most 48 integers in [1,512], with no element the mean of any subset of at least two distinct OTHER elements. Exact subset-sum dynamic programming verifies all subset sizes.

science-nondividing-three-other-sums-192.rationale: The candidate constructs at most 48 distinct integers in [1,192] in which no element divides the sum of three distinct other elements; the evaluator checks every such triple exactly, and the size of the set is maximized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_nondividing_k_sum, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: No element dividing a sum of three others
evidence.description: construct() -> 1..maximum=48 distinct positive integers <=n=192. No selected integer may divide the sum of any k=3 DISTINCT OTHER selected integers. Maximize cardinality. This excludes the tested element from the summands. Follow the prize bank’s prescribed-number wording: k=3 distinct OTHER summands in [1,192], at most 48 elements. This relaxes the broader all-subsets condition in Erdős’s survey and is not attributed as his exact original statement.

science-number-theory-bounded-lcm.rationale: The candidate returns a subset of [1, 512] in which every pair has least common multiple at most 512; the evaluator checks all pairs with exact integer arithmetic and scores the cardinality. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_bounded_lcm, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large integer sets with bounded pairwise least common multiples
evidence.description: Return a nonempty subset of [1,512] with lcm(a,b)<=512 for every pair. Maximize cardinality. Finite instance of the extremal bounded-lcm problem. The simple seed does not import Chen's asymptotic construction.

science-number-theory-convex-primes.rationale: The candidate returns an increasing sequence of primes up to 10000 whose successive gaps never decrease; the evaluator checks primality by trial division and the gap condition, and scores the length. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_convex_primes, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Long increasing prime sequences with nondecreasing gaps
evidence.description: Return increasing prime integers <=10000 with successive gaps NONDECREASING. Maximize length; these are arbitrary prime subsequences, not consecutive primes. Finite inverse form of the growth-rate question for convex prime subsequences; keeps the source non-strict gap inequality.

science-number-theory-coprime-sumset.rationale: The candidate returns two 3-element subsets A, B of [1, 128] whose sumset has pairwise coprime elements; the evaluator checks every pair of sums by gcd and scores the number of distinct sums. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_coprime_sumset, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large pairwise-coprime sumsets of two bounded integer sets
evidence.description: Return two lists A,B, each containing exactly 3 distinct integers in [1,128]. All DISTINCT values in A+B must be pairwise coprime. Maximize the cardinality of A+B; repeated representations are allowed. Finite construction model for the Straus sumset-density question. Three elements per summand set and the bounding box are local; finite cardinality does not establish infinite density.

science-number-theory-dissociated-recipr.rationale: The candidate returns a subset of [1, 22] whose reciprocals have pairwise distinct subset sums; the evaluator enumerates all subset sums over a common denominator and scores the cardinality. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_dissociated_reciprocals, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Reciprocal sets with all subset sums distinct
evidence.description: Return a nonempty subset of [1,22] such that ALL reciprocal subset sums, including the empty sum, are distinct. Maximize cardinality. Maximizes the size of a dissociated reciprocal set. This is not the counting task for all harmonic subset sums.

science-number-theory-egyptian-long.rationale: The candidate returns distinct denominators in [5, 10^7] whose reciprocals sum to exactly 1; the evaluator checks the sum in exact rational arithmetic and scores the number of terms, which is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_egyptian_long, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Few-term Egyptian fractions with denominators greater than four
evidence.description: Return 1..256 distinct integer denominators in [5,10000000] whose reciprocal sum is exactly 1; minimize their count. Minimize the number of distinct unit fractions representing one with all denominators above a fixed threshold; denominator and term caps are local.

science-number-theory-egyptian-maximum.rationale: The candidate returns distinct denominators whose reciprocals sum to exactly 5/31; the evaluator checks the sum in exact rational arithmetic and scores the largest denominator, which is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_egyptian_maximum, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Small largest denominator in an Egyptian expansion of 5/31
evidence.description: Return 1..256 distinct denominators in [1,10000000] summing reciprocally to exactly 5/31. Minimize the LARGEST denominator, not the term count. One fixed rational instance of the denominator-size problem; the paper provides asymptotic bounds, not this local benchmark optimum.

science-number-theory-equal-gcd-free.rationale: The candidate returns a subset of [1, 128] with no three elements whose pairwise greatest common divisors are all equal; the evaluator checks every triple exactly and scores the cardinality. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_equal_gcd_free, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large integer sets avoiding equal-gcd triples
evidence.description: Return nonempty subset of [1,128] with no three distinct elements whose three pairwise greatest common divisors are equal. Maximize cardinality. The finite f_r(x) extremal function for r=3, not merely pairwise coprimality avoidance.

science-number-theory-equal-lcm-free.rationale: The candidate returns a subset of [1, 128] with no three elements whose pairwise least common multiples are all equal; the evaluator checks every triple exactly and scores the cardinality. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_equal_lcm_free, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large integer sets avoiding equal-lcm triples
evidence.description: Return nonempty subset of [1,128] containing no three distinct elements whose three pairwise least common multiples are equal. Maximize cardinality. Finite extremal version of the equal-lcm-triple density question. Distinct from the equal-gcd and bounded-lcm objectives.

science-number-theory-factorial-large-fa.rationale: The candidate returns distinct integers greater than 12 whose product is exactly 12!; the evaluator multiplies them exactly and scores the largest factor, which is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_factorial_large_factors, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Factorial decompositions into distinct factors above the index
evidence.description: Return 1..12 DISTINCT integers all greater than 12, with product exactly 12!. Minimize the LARGEST factor; the number of factors is variable. Exact finite version of equation (6). Distinct from the existing 100! benchmark: no fixed factor count, all factors must exceed 12, and the objective minimizes the largest rather than maximizing the smallest.

science-number-theory-factorial-valuatio.rationale: The candidate returns a set of indices in [2, 32] containing 2; the evaluator sums the corresponding factorials exactly and scores the 2-adic valuation of the sum, which is maximized. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_factorial_valuation, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: High two-adic valuation of factorial sums containing 2!
evidence.description: Return a distinct subset of factorial indices [2,32] containing 2. Maximize v2(sum(i!)); the smallest index is FIXED at 2 to match the source question f(a1,p). Fixes the smallest factorial index as required by the original valuation question. The seed is a local greedy algorithm; any known numerical identity it rediscovers is not a novel result.

science-number-theory-inverse-free-inter.rationale: The candidate returns an interval inside [1, 1008] that contains no two residues (equal ones included) whose product is 1 modulo 1009; the evaluator checks the modular inverse of every element and scores the interval length. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_inverse_free_interval, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Long intervals containing no modular inverse pair
evidence.description: Return [start,length] for a nonempty interval contained in [1,1008]. For EVERY x,y in the interval, including x=y, require x*y %1009 !=1. Maximize interval length. Finite obstruction search for the modular inverse-pair interval question. Diagonal pairs are checked, so the self-inverse residues 1 and 1008 cannot be present; this is stricter than the preliminary distinct-pair proposal.

science-number-theory-lcm-reciprocal-wei.rationale: The candidate returns a subset of [2, 256] in which every pair has least common multiple above 256; the evaluator checks all pairs exactly and scores the exact rational sum of reciprocals, which is maximized. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_lcm_reciprocal_weight, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large reciprocal weight under lcm separation
evidence.description: Return nonempty subset of [2,256] with lcm(a,b)>256 for all distinct pairs. Maximize exact reciprocal sum, not cardinality. Uses the reciprocal-sum objective in section 14(1), with n fixed; pairwise lcm threshold is strict and the score is rational. The unit denominator 1 is excluded locally to remove its isolated trivial certificate.

science-number-theory-noncoprime-forced.rationale: The candidate returns a subset of [1, 255] that contains 255 and has no coprime pair; the evaluator checks every pair by gcd and scores the cardinality. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_noncoprime_forced, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large pairwise noncoprime sets containing the interval endpoint
evidence.description: Return a nonempty subset of [1,255] containing 255, with gcd(a,b)>1 for all distinct pairs. Maximize cardinality. Fixes n=255 in g(n), the source's exact forced-maximum-element formulation; no solution to a general coprime-family conjecture is claimed.

science-number-theory-pair-sum-nondivisi.rationale: The candidate returns a subset of [1, 256] in which a+b never divides a*b for distinct elements; the evaluator checks every pair with integer arithmetic and scores the cardinality. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_pair_sum_nondivisibility, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Integer sets whose pair sums never divide pair products
evidence.description: Return a nonempty subset of [1,256]. For every distinct a,b require (a*b)%(a+b)!=0. Maximize cardinality. The prescribed distinct-pair divisibility exclusion does not require the quotient to belong to the selected set, unlike the reciprocal Schur task. The source writes x,y without explicitly excluding equality; this implementation follows the bank's stated distinct-pair variant.

science-number-theory-power-residue-run.rationale: The candidate returns a start s and five square roots certifying that s, ..., s+4 are quadratic residues modulo 1009; the evaluator squares each root modulo 1009 and scores s, which is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_power_residue_run, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Early runs of five quadratic residues modulo 1009
evidence.description: Return {'start':s,'roots':[r0,...,r4]}, with 1<=s<=1004 and 1<=ri<=1008. Require ri**2 mod 1009 == s+i. Minimize s; zero residues and wraparound are excluded. A fixed-prime instance of the least run-start r(k,m,p), with k=2 and m=5. Each residue is certified by its root; no limsup over primes is computed.

science-number-theory-powerful-consecuti.rationale: The candidate returns an integer n below 10^12 with complete prime factorizations of n and n+1 showing that both are powerful and neither is a square; the evaluator checks primality, the products and the non-square condition exactly and gives a valid certificate the score 1. Reviewed source family science_prize_powerful, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Consecutive powerful non-squares: exact counterexample certificate
evidence.description: Provide a positive integer n and complete prime factorizations certifying that n and n+1 are powerful and neither is a square. Every prime exponent must be at least two. The verifier uses exact integers and primality tests. This recreates the resolved yes/no question in JSP-000301, with a local certificate-size bound n+1 <= 10^12 and binary validity score. The published witness is explicitly credited to Solomon W. Golomb.

science-number-theory-powerful-parts.rationale: The candidate returns one integer n in [10^4, 10^6]; the evaluator factors n and n+1 by trial division and scores the product of their powerful parts, which is maximized. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_powerful_parts, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large powerful-part product for consecutive integers
evidence.description: Return an integer n in [10000,1000000]. Its powerful part is the product of FULL prime powers p^e with exponent e>=2 in its factorization. Maximize powerful_part(n)*powerful_part(n+1). The B2 powerful-part construction allows squarefree factors and does not require either whole integer to be powerful or nonsquare; distinct from the existing Golomb counterexample certificate.

science-number-theory-reciprocal-schur-f.rationale: The candidate returns a subset of [1, 180] with no three distinct elements satisfying 1/a = 1/b + 1/c; the evaluator tests every pair b, c with integer arithmetic and scores the cardinality. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_reciprocal_schur_free, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large sets avoiding reciprocal Schur triples
evidence.description: Return a nonempty subset of [1,180] with no THREE DISTINCT elements a,b,c satisfying 1/a=1/b+1/c. Maximize cardinality. Three-distinct-element specialization of the reciprocal equation, weaker than forbidding arbitrary reciprocal subsums.

science-number-theory-reciprocal-subset-.rationale: The candidate returns a subset of [1, 24] in which no reciprocal equals a sum of reciprocals of other selected elements; the evaluator runs an exact subset-sum check for every element and scores the cardinality. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_reciprocal_subset_free, area mathematics.

evidence.description: Return a nonempty subset of [1,24]; no reciprocal of a selected element may equal the sum of reciprocals of a subset of the OTHER selected elements. Maximize cardinality. Finite version of the extremal S* question; operands are distinct selected elements and the target is excluded from its own subsum.

science-number-theory-sidon-obstruction.rationale: The candidate returns 12 distinct integers in [0, 128]; the evaluator finds the largest Sidon subset by exhaustive search and scores its size, which is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_sidon_obstruction, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Ambient integer sets with small largest Sidon subset
evidence.description: Return exactly 12 distinct integers in [0,128]. Evaluator exhaustively computes the largest subset with all unordered pair sums unique INCLUDING diagonals. MINIMIZE that maximum subset size. The candidate chooses a hard AMBIENT set; the evaluator solves Sidon extraction exactly. This reverses the outer optimization compared with constructing a large Sidon set in a fixed interval.

science-number-theory-signed-harmonic.rationale: The candidate returns 30 coefficients in {-1, 0, 1}; the evaluator computes the signed harmonic sum exactly, rejects zero, and scores its absolute value, which is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_signed_harmonic, area mathematics.

evidence.description: Return exactly 30 integer coefficients from {-1,0,1}. The signed sum coefficient[i-1]/i must be nonzero. Minimize its absolute value; exact numerator and denominator are reported. Finite signed-harmonic extremum with the zero sum excluded; no asymptotic separation claim.

science-number-theory-smooth-adjacent.rationale: The candidate returns one integer n in [10^4, 10^6]; the evaluator factors n and n+1 by trial division and scores the largest prime factor of n(n+1), which is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_smooth_adjacent, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Small largest prime factor of consecutive-integer products
evidence.description: Return integer n in [10000,1000000]. Minimize the largest prime factor of n(n+1), independently computed by exact trial division. Searches a bounded window for smooth consecutive integers. The local lower cutoff prevents the trivial pair 1,2; it proves no asymptotic bound.

science-number-theory-smooth-decompositi.rationale: The candidate returns two positive integers summing to 123457; the evaluator factors both by trial division and scores the larger of their largest prime factors, which is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_smooth_decomposition, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Smooth two-summand decomposition of a prescribed integer
evidence.description: Return two positive integers a,b with a+b=123457. Minimize max(P(a),P(b)), where P is the largest prime factor and P(1)=1. The evaluator factors both integers independently. One fixed-target version of the small-prime-factor additive decomposition question; no universal bound for all large integers is asserted.

science-number-theory-smooth-parts.rationale: The candidate returns one integer n in [10^3, 10^6]; the evaluator extracts from each of n+1, ..., n+24 the part composed of primes below 24 and scores the number of distinct parts, which is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_smooth_parts, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Few distinct small-prime parts in a short integer interval
evidence.description: Return n in [1000,1000000]. For each n+i,1<=i<=24, extract its complete factor composed of primes STRICTLY BELOW 24. MINIMIZE the number of distinct extracted factors. Uses the source minimum f(n,t) at t=24, correcting the preliminary feasibility proposal's reversed direction; the source asks for a uniform lower bound on this minimum.

science-number-theory-square-sum-free.rationale: The candidate returns a subset of [1, 256] in which no sum of two elements (an element with itself included) is a perfect square; the evaluator checks every pair with integer square roots and scores the cardinality. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_square_sum_free, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Integer sets avoiding square pair sums, including diagonals
evidence.description: Return nonempty subset of [1,256] such that a+b is never a perfect square for a<=b in the set, INCLUDING a=b. Maximize cardinality. Explicit diagonal-including restriction resolves the terse bank wording; all pairs are verified with integer square roots. It is distinct from square DIFFERENCE avoidance.

science-number-theory-target-subsum-free.rationale: The candidate returns a subset of [1, 100] with no subset summing to 200; the evaluator runs an exact subset-sum computation and scores the cardinality. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_target_subsum_free, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large interval sets avoiding a prescribed subset sum
evidence.description: Return a nonempty subset of [1,100] with no subset summing to 200. Maximize cardinality. Each element can occur at most once in the forbidden sum. Fixes the target and ambient interval in the question about integers below n/k avoiding a subset sum n; the inclusive endpoint convention is local.

science-number-theory-totient-multiple.rationale: The candidate returns one integer n up to 10^6 whose Euler totient is divisible by 120; the evaluator factors n, computes the totient exactly and scores n, which is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_totient_multiple, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Small integer whose totient is divisible by 120
evidence.description: Return integer n in [1,1000000] with phi(n) divisible by 120. Minimize n; the evaluator independently factors n and computes the exact totient. Constructs m_n from the source by fixing its divisor parameter to 120; does not compare asymptotic ratios with least primes in progressions.

science-number-theory-unique-block-produ.rationale: The candidate returns an increasing sequence of integers in [2, 128] whose consecutive blocks all have distinct products; the evaluator computes every block product exactly and scores the length. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_unique_block_products, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Dense increasing sequences with unique block products
evidence.description: Return strictly increasing integers in [2,128]. Products of every nonempty consecutive block must be distinct. Maximize length; singleton products are included. Finite restriction of the density-one sequence question. The implementation neither verifies nor relies on the bank's unverified modern solution/priority claims.

science-number-theory-unique-interval-su.rationale: The candidate returns an increasing sequence of integers in [1, 256] whose consecutive blocks all have distinct sums; the evaluator computes every block sum and scores the length. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_unique_interval_sums, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Increasing sequences with unique consecutive-block sums
evidence.description: Return a strictly increasing sequence of integers in [1,256]. Sums of all nonempty consecutive blocks must be distinct. Maximize sequence length. Finite version of the Erdős–Harzheim increasing-sequence question. Only consecutive blocks, not arbitrary subsets, must have distinct sums.

science-number-theory-unit-fraction-pack.rationale: The candidate selects denominators from 2, ..., 48 whose reciprocals sum to strictly less than 1; the evaluator computes the sum in exact rational arithmetic and scores the gap to 1, which is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_b_unit_fraction_packing, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Closest strict underpacking of one by supplied unit fractions
evidence.description: Return nonempty distinct zero-based indices into denominators [2,3,...,48]; reciprocal sum must be STRICTLY BELOW 1. Minimize positive deficit 1-sum; exact rational value is reported. Fixed finite input collection whose reciprocal total exceeds one; minimizes the strict deficit rather than asserting a uniform bound for all collections. The source permits an exact-one subsum; the local protocol explicitly excludes it.

science-odd-covering-divisors-of-51975.rationale: The candidate assigns residue classes to distinct odd divisors of 51975; the evaluator counts exactly the residues modulo 51975 that no class covers. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_odd_covering, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Odd covering systems with moduli dividing 51975 (fewest uncovered residues)
evidence.description: construct() -> classes [[m, r], ...] with distinct moduli m > 1 dividing 51975 = 3^3 * 5^2 * 7 * 11 (hence odd) and 0 <= r < m. The score is the number of residues modulo 51975 covered by no class (exact). Minimize. The score 0 (a covering system with distinct odd moduli) is impossible for this modulus by the necessary condition of Berger, Felzenbaum and Fraenkel (1986). Every divisor of 51975 above 1 is available once. The minimum is positive: an odd covering with distinct moduli needs prod (p-1)/(p-2) - sum 1/(p-2) > 2 over the primes p dividing the least common multiple (Berger, Felzenbaum and Fraenkel), and for 3, 5, 7, 11 the left side is 86/45. The score measures how close systems with this modulus come to a covering; it cannot decide the odd covering problem. No minimum is documented.

science-one-repeated-sum-100.rationale: The candidate returns a subset of {1..100}; the evaluator checks that at most one value has more than one representation as a sum of two elements and scores the size. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_one_repeated_sum, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Subsets of {1, ..., 100} in which at most one sum is repeated
evidence.description: construct() -> distinct integers in 1..100 such that at most one integer has more than one representation a + b with a <= b in the set. Maximize the size; the optimum is 16. For N = 100 the maximum is 16, so the task recovers an extremal set.

science-oppositely-ordered-farey-pair-10.rationale: The candidate returns two Farey fractions of order 1000 whose numerators and denominators change in opposite directions. The evaluator scores the difference of their ranks in the Farey sequence. Reviewed source family science_prize_d_opposite_farey_pair, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Nearby oppositely ordered fractions in the Farey sequence
evidence.description: construct() -> [[a,b],[c,d]], two reduced fractions in [0,1] with denominators <=1000, a/b<c/d, and (c-a)*(d-b)<0. Minimize their rank difference in the complete Farey sequence of order 1000, including 0/1 and 1/1. Every rank is recomputed exactly. The local finite search gives an upper certificate for the first possible ordering failure at order 1000. It corrects the feasibility draft's unrelated strictly monotone-run objective. The optimum is 252, found by scanning the complete Farey sequence of order 1000; this is a rediscovery task.

science-orchard-twelve-rational-points.rationale: The candidate returns 12 integer points; the evaluator finds all lines through the points with exact integer arithmetic and scores the number containing exactly three points, which is maximized. Reviewed source family science_prize_g_orchard, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Twelve rational points with many three-point lines (orchard problem)
evidence.description: construct() -> exactly 12 distinct integer points [x, y] with |x|, |y| <= 10^30 (any rational configuration can be scaled to integers). Maximize the number of lines containing exactly three of the points, computed exactly; the optimum is 19. The real maximum for 12 points is 19, and the group law on a rational cubic with 12-torsion realizes it with rational points, so the rational optimum is also 19.

science-ordinary-lines-twelve-rational-p.rationale: The candidate returns 12 integer points, not all on one line; the evaluator finds all lines through the points with exact integer arithmetic and scores the number containing exactly two points, which is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_g_ordinary_lines, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Twelve rational points with few ordinary lines
evidence.description: construct() -> exactly 12 distinct integer points [x, y] with |x|, |y| <= 10^9, not all collinear. Minimize the number of lines containing exactly two of the points (exact). Over the reals the minimum for 12 points is 6 and integer coordinates reach it, so the optimum is 6.

science-pair-sum-prime-diversity-12.rationale: The candidate constructs 12 distinct positive integers at most 10000; the evaluator factors every sum of two distinct elements exactly and counts the distinct primes that occur, which is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_pair_sum_prime_diversity, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Few prime factors across pairwise sums
evidence.description: construct() -> n=12 distinct positive integers <=maximum=10000. Factor every sum of two DISTINCT elements, union all prime factors and minimize the number of distinct primes. Choose 12 distinct positive integers at most 10000; minimize the number of distinct primes dividing sums of distinct-index pairs. Equal-index sums are excluded.

science-paired-sidon-disjoint-difference.rationale: The candidate constructs two Sidon subsets of [1,256] whose nonzero difference sets do not intersect; the evaluator verifies both conditions exactly, and the combined size is maximized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_paired_sidon, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Two Sidon sets with disjoint difference sets
evidence.description: construct() -> [A,B], two nonempty Sidon subsets of [1,n=256], at most 64 elements each. Pair sums inside each set, including a+a, must be unique. Their nonzero difference sets must be disjoint. Maximize |A|+|B|; A and B need not themselves be disjoint. Two Sidon subsets of [1,256]; maximize combined size and require disjoint nonzero differences. Ordinary Sidon diagonals are included, and the two sets themselves may overlap.

science-pairwise-sum-triple-free-sets.rationale: The candidate returns a set of integers in 1..128. The evaluator checks that no three members have all three pairwise sums in the set and scores the set size. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_717, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large sets without a triple and all its pair sums
evidence.description: construct() -> distinct integers in 1..128. Forbid THREE DISTINCT members a,b,c for which a+b, a+c and b+c are also selected. The six displayed values need not be mutually distinct. Maximize set size. The local interval ends at 128. The evaluator uses only exact finite checks and does not assume the preprint’s proof, novelty, status, or Lean verification. The baseline is the elementary upper half interval.

science-pancyclic-graph-excess-40.rationale: The candidate returns a 40-vertex graph with one explicit cycle of every length from 3 to 40. The evaluator checks every cycle and scores the number of edges beyond 40. Reviewed source family science_prize_d_pancyclic, area mathematics.

evidence.description: construct() -> {'edges': undirected edge pairs on vertices 0..39, 'cycles': one vertex-list cycle of every length 3..40 in that order}. Edges are simple and distinct; cycle vertices are distinct and every required edge must exist. Minimize edge count minus 40. This is an independently implemented n=40 construction search with explicit cycle certificates. The seed is an elementary fan graph, not a copied minimal construction.

science-particle-collider-anomaly-rankin.rationale: The source specifies physical-event reconstruction, a physical surrogate, decoding, imaging or parameter inference. The scientific target, not use of a learned model, determines the primary domain. Reviewed source family science_physics_lhco_control_region_anomalies, area particle_physics.

evidence.description: fit(control_features) -> object with score(events). Input consists of pinned physics features derived from official LHCO Pythia/Delphes events; candidate never receives signal truth. Independent training, test and no-signal source event blocks. Score SIC at 5 percent background divided by one plus mass-sculpting chi-square. Report no-signal acceptance and AUROC; no discovery p value.

science-particle-helical-track-reconstru.rationale: The source specifies physical-event reconstruction, a physical surrogate, decoding, imaging or parameter inference. The scientific target, not use of a learned model, determines the primary domain. Reviewed source family science_physics_trackml_complete_events, area particle_physics.

evidence.description: assign_tracks(hits, cells, metadata) -> integer track ID for each hit. Input retains complete official TrackML events, source cells and detector geometry. Whole events split, no truth supplied. Score exact strict two-sided majority TrackML weighted score. No artificial helices or hit subsampling.

science-penny-graph-contacts-32.rationale: The candidate returns 32 distinct points of the triangular lattice; the evaluator counts the pairs at distance exactly one with integer arithmetic, which is maximized. Reviewed source family science_prize_g_penny, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Contact numbers of 32 unit pennies on the triangular lattice
evidence.description: construct() -> exactly 32 distinct integer pairs [a, b] with |a|, |b| <= 64 denoting lattice points a + b*omega, omega = exp(i*pi/3), which are at mutual distance at least one. Maximize the number of pairs at distance exactly one; Harborth's theorem gives the optimum floor(3n - sqrt(12n - 3)) = 76. Harborth's formula gives 76 for n = 32 and triangular-lattice spirals attain it, so the lattice restriction loses nothing.

science-pentagon-hexagon-free-extremal-4.rationale: The candidate returns the edge list of a graph on 42 vertices; the evaluator searches exactly for five-cycles and six-cycles and scores the number of edges. Reviewed source family science_prize_f_pentagon_hexagon_free, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Graphs on 42 vertices without five- or six-cycles
evidence.description: construct() -> list of edges [u, v] of a simple graph on vertices 0..41 containing neither a five-cycle nor a six-cycle. Maximize the number of edges; the known optimum is 104. The exact value 104 for n = 42 is known; the task recovers it.

science-permutation-monotone-progression.rationale: The candidate constructs a permutation of 1 to 128; the evaluator computes exactly the longest subsequence whose values form an increasing or decreasing arithmetic progression, which is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_permutation_progression, area mathematics.

evidence.description: construct() -> a permutation of 1..n=128. Minimize the longest subsequence whose values form an increasing OR decreasing nonconstant arithmetic progression; subsequence positions need not be adjacent. A known finite construction attains 2, so this is a rediscovery task. Permute [1,128] and minimize the longest arithmetic-progression subsequence, allowing either sign of the common difference. The known finite optimum is 2; infinite-permutation questions are not recreated here.

science-physics-ariel-atmospheric-poster.rationale: The source specifies physical-event reconstruction, a physical surrogate, decoding, imaging or parameter inference. The scientific target, not use of a learned model, determines the primary domain. Reviewed source family science_physics_ariel_atmospheric_posterior, area cosmology_and_astrophysics.

evidence.description: retrieve(spectrum, uncertainty, planet_metadata) -> 32..4096 integer indices into source TauREx forward grid, with repetition. Metadata carries physical parameters, opacity-pinned spectra and prior bounds. Posterior is a declared discrete-grid adaptation. Score generating-truth CRPS, agreement with released nested-sampling reference posterior and independent spectral predictive likelihood. Split entire planets and atmospheric regimes.

science-physics-broadband-antireflection.rationale: The candidate designs a stack of low- and high-index layers on glass under layer-count and thickness limits. The evaluator checks the limits and computes the mean reflectance over 400-800 nm with the thin-film characteristic-matrix method. Reviewed source family physics_research_antireflection_coating, area physics.

evidence.description: Design a stack of at most twenty low- and high-index layers (1.38 and 2.35) on glass that minimizes the mean reflectance between 400 and 800 nm at normal incidence, with at most 1000 nm of total coating. The evaluator checks the constraints and computes the reflectance spectrum exactly with the thin-film characteristic-matrix method.

science-physics-calochallenge-photon-sho.rationale: The source specifies physical-event reconstruction, a physical surrogate, decoding, imaging or parameter inference. The scientific target, not use of a learned model, determines the primary domain. Reviewed source family science_physics_calochallenge_photon_showers, area particle_physics.

evidence.description: fit_showers(training) -> sampler(incident_energies, rng). Training contains showers, incident_energies and voxel geometry from official CaloChallenge Dataset 1 photons. Return nonnegative (event,voxel) deposits in MeV. Independent source-file events are held out. Score per-energy standardized Wasserstein of shower response, sparsity, layer fractions, centroids and widths. Classifier AUC and generation time are separate diagnostics. Compact CPU adaptation, not full challenge leaderboard.

science-physics-cnot-budgeted-unitary-sy.rationale: The candidate compiles seven fixed two- and three-qubit unitaries into single-qubit rotations and CNOT gates within stated CNOT budgets. The evaluator rebuilds each circuit's unitary and scores the mean phase-insensitive distance to the targets. Reviewed source family physics_research_unitary_synthesis, area quantum_information.

evidence.task_name: Physics: exact quantum circuit synthesis within published CNOT budgets
evidence.description: Compile seven fixed two- and three-qubit unitaries (CNOT, iSWAP, SWAP, the Toffoli gate and three generic unitaries) into single-qubit rotations and CNOT gates without exceeding the CNOT counts known to suffice for each. The evaluator rebuilds every circuit's unitary exactly and scores the mean phase-insensitive distance to the targets.

science-physics-experimental-surface-cod.rationale: The source specifies physical-event reconstruction, a physical surrogate, decoding, imaging or parameter inference. The scientific target, not use of a learned model, determines the primary domain. Reviewed source family science_physics_experimental_surface_code, area quantum_information.

evidence.description: decode(detector_events, metadata) -> shot x observable bits. Metadata includes source detector-error model, code distance and observable count. Train/test acquisition batches disjoint. Score logical failure per complete experimental shot, with Wilson confidence interval and timing. PyMatching baseline uses only error model and detector events.

science-physics-freegsnke-coil-design.rationale: The candidate constructs bounded coil-current settings for a specified plasma boundary; this is physical configuration design, not a robot policy. Reviewed source family science_physics_freegsnke_coil_design, area physics.

evidence.description: design_coils(machine, target_boundary, plasma_profile) -> eight bounded active-coil currents in A for the published Anamak geometry. Evaluator runs pinned FreeGSNKE static equilibrium at two grid resolutions, checks nonlinear Grad-Shafranov residual, closed-plasma topology and current bounds, then scores boundary/axis mismatch. Targets/profile cases generated from the specified source model and saved with numerical reference checks. No physical reactor claim.

science-physics-great3-shear-calibration.rationale: The source specifies physical-event reconstruction, a physical surrogate, decoding, imaging or parameter inference. The scientific target, not use of a learned model, determines the primary domain. Reviewed source family science_physics_great3_shear_calibration, area cosmology_and_astrophysics.

evidence.description: estimate_shear(images, psf, metadata) -> [g1,g2] per GREAT3 subfield. Images have (galaxy,y,x) axes; PSF is a source stamp. Noise-cancellation groups remain intact. Independent evaluator rotates shear into PSF frame and computes official ground constant-shear Qc with multiplicative/additive bias diagnostics. No variable-shear claim.

science-physics-heisenberg-product-formu.rationale: The candidate chooses the coefficients of a twelve-stage product formula for the time evolution of a six-site Heisenberg chain. The evaluator builds the product and the exact propagator and scores the mean spectral-norm error at three evolution times. Reviewed source family physics_research_trotter_splitting, area quantum_information.

evidence.task_name: Physics: product-formula design for Heisenberg-chain time evolution
evidence.description: Choose the coefficients of a twelve-stage product formula that approximates the time evolution of a six-site Heisenberg chain split into even and odd bonds. The evaluator builds every factor and the exact propagator and scores the mean spectral-norm error at three evolution times.

science-physics-jhtdb-subgrid-stress.rationale: The source specifies physical-event reconstruction, a physical surrogate, decoding, imaging or parameter inference. The scientific target, not use of a learned model, determines the primary domain. Reviewed source family science_physics_jhtdb_subgrid_stress, area physics.

evidence.description: closure(filtered_velocity, gradients, filter_width) -> N x N x N x 3 x 3 symmetric subgrid stress. Complete periodic source DNS boxes (not wrapped cutouts) supply independent box-filtered ground truth. Whole space-time blocks split. Score stress and energy-transfer errors plus Fourier energy error after evaluator RK2 coarse rollout. Galilean and cyclic rotational consistency and rollout stability required.

science-physics-mlgwsc-event-search.rationale: The candidate detects and ranks events in gravitational-wave strain signals under a false-alarm constraint. Reviewed source family science_physics_mlgwsc_event_search, area cosmology_and_astrophysics.

evidence.description: search(h1, l1, metadata) -> N x 2 GPS time/ranking statistic array. Independent source observing blocks and source injections; triggers clustered and uniquely associated. Score sensitive distance at fixed FAR. At least 10 expected false alarms at the declared FAR must fit in the background duration; tiny noise clips cannot establish rare-event performance.

science-physics-ngeht-closure-imaging.rationale: The source specifies physical-event reconstruction, a physical surrogate, decoding, imaging or parameter inference. The scientific target, not use of a learned model, determines the primary domain. Reviewed source family science_physics_ngeht_closure_imaging, area cosmology_and_astrophysics.

evidence.description: reconstruct(visibilities, array_metadata, noise) -> nonnegative square image in Jy per pixel with calibrated total flux. Source data supply uv wavelengths, amplitudes, signed closure triangles and phases. Independent direct Fourier transform checks amplitude/closure likelihood and fixed-centre, resolution-matched image NRMSE. Source models/schedules split. Official ngEHT permission required before staging restricted challenge files.

science-physics-nuclear-mass-extrapolati.rationale: The candidate fits a nuclear mass model on the AME2016 experimental masses and predicts the mass excesses of 71 nuclides first measured afterwards. The evaluator scores the root-mean-square deviation from the withheld AME2020 values. Reviewed source family physics_research_nuclear_mass_extrapolation, area physics.

evidence.task_name: Physics: predicting newly measured nuclear masses from the AME2016 evaluation
evidence.description: Fit a nuclear mass model on the experimental masses of the 2016 Atomic Mass Evaluation and predict the mass excesses of the 71 nuclides first measured in time for AME2020. The candidate never sees the AME2020 values, and the score is the root-mean-square deviation from them in keV.

science-physics-photonic-crystal-tm-band.rationale: The candidate draws a symmetric 32x32-pixel unit cell of air and dielectric for a square-lattice photonic crystal. The evaluator computes the TM band structure with a plane-wave method and scores the gap-midgap ratio between the fourth and fifth bands. Reviewed source family physics_research_photonic_band_gap, area physics.

evidence.task_name: Physics: photonic-crystal unit cell with a large higher-order TM band gap
evidence.description: Design a symmetric 32x32-pixel unit cell of air and dielectric (epsilon 12) for a two-dimensional square-lattice photonic crystal that opens the largest gap between the fourth and fifth TM bands. The evaluator solves the band structure with an exact-coefficient plane-wave method over the irreducible Brillouin zone and scores the gap-midgap ratio.

science-physics-refnx-contrast-inversion.rationale: The source specifies physical-event reconstruction, a physical surrogate, decoding, imaging or parameter inference. The scientific target, not use of a learned model, determines the primary domain. Reviewed source family science_physics_refnx_contrast_inversion, area physics.

evidence.description: infer_profile(training_contrasts, bounds, metadata) -> 32..4096 posterior rows [oxide thickness A, film thickness A, dry film SLD 1e-6/A^2, solvent fraction, roughness A, background]. Independent Parratt recursion with Nevot-Croce roughness and Gaussian Q-resolution predicts the wholly held-out contrast. Score posterior predictive normalized residual plus simulation-track CRPS. Source experimental contrasts are one physical sample, no cross-sample generalization claim.

science-physics-robust-transmon-control.rationale: The candidate designs a constrained control pulse for a transmon gate and is scored through a fixed quantum-dynamics simulation. Reviewed source family science_physics_robust_transmon_control, area quantum_information.

evidence.description: pulse(target_gate, hardware_model) -> (80,2) IQ amplitudes rad/ns for 40 ns X-pi gate in a three-level Duffing transmon. Enforce amplitude .4 rad/ns and slew .12 rad/ns/ns including endpoints. Independent Lindblad expm and refined DOP853 evaluate six Bloch states over 3x3 detuning/calibration cases, relaxation and dephasing. Score mean plus worst average gate infidelity; report leakage. Explicit simulation, not QuOCS benchmark reproduction.

science-physics-spin-glass-torus-2d.rationale: The candidate is a ground-state search routine that returns spin configurations for nine two-dimensional periodic Ising spin-glass instances within a CPU budget. The evaluator recomputes each cut weight and scores the mean ratio to the tabulated optimal cut. Reviewed source family physics_research_spin_glass_torus_2d, area physics.

evidence.task_name: Physics: two-dimensional spin-glass ground states on fixed instances
evidence.description: Find ground states of nine Edwards-Anderson spin glasses on 10x10, 15x15 and 20x20 periodic square lattices with Gaussian couplings. The evaluator recomputes the cut weight of every returned spin configuration and compares it with the exact optimum computed for these instances by branch-and-cut.

science-physics-spin-glass-torus-3d.rationale: The candidate is a ground-state search routine that returns spin configurations for nine three-dimensional periodic Ising spin-glass instances within a CPU budget. The evaluator recomputes each cut weight and scores the mean ratio to the tabulated optimal cut. Reviewed source family physics_research_spin_glass_torus_3d, area physics.

evidence.task_name: Physics: three-dimensional spin-glass ground states on fixed instances
evidence.description: Find ground states of nine Edwards-Anderson spin glasses on 5x5x5, 6x6x6 and 7x7x7 periodic cubic lattices with Gaussian couplings. The evaluator recomputes the cut weight of every spin configuration and compares it with the exact optimum computed for these instances by branch-and-cut.

science-physics-tdlmc-distance-posterior.rationale: The source specifies physical-event reconstruction, a physical surrogate, decoding, imaging or parameter inference. The scientific target, not use of a learned model, determines the primary domain. Reviewed source family science_physics_tdlmc_distance_posterior, area cosmology_and_astrophysics.

evidence.description: infer_distance(image, psf, time_delays, kinematics, metadata) -> 32..4096 joint physical posterior samples; first column time-delay distance Mpc, others named bounded lens/source nuisances. Metadata includes evaluator-owned lenstronomy forward callable and budget. TDLMC Rungs 1 or 2 whole systems only. Relative distance CRPS plus independent image/delay/dynamical forward-likelihood penalty; bias, interval width and coverage reported.

science-physics-xy-critical-monte-carlo.rationale: The candidate specifies a quadrature rule or sampling schedule for a physical numerical calculation; accuracy is evaluated under the declared work constraints. Reviewed source family science_physics_xy_critical_monte_carlo, area physics.

evidence.description: schedule(temperature, lattice_size, budget) -> list of 1..64 kernel names: metropolis, overrelax, wolff, containing a stochastic kernel. Trusted detailed-balance kernels operate classical periodic XY model. Each sweep/cluster is charged N site units (upper bound); warmup counts. Multiple independent chains score squared energy/magnetization errors against long independent reference chains, with reference uncertainty and autocorrelation diagnostics. Fixed-work local adaptation, not a timing leaderboard.

science-planar-bipartite-list-colouring.rationale: The candidate returns a colouring for each of four fixed seeded planar bipartite graphs whose vertices carry lists of three colours; the evaluator regenerates the graphs and lists and scores the number of instances coloured properly from the lists. Reviewed source family science_prize_i_planar_list_colouring, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Colouring four fixed planar bipartite graphs from lists of three colours
evidence.description: construct() -> four colourings, one per instance from planar_bipartite_lists(splits, seed) for (20,701), (40,702), (60,703), (100,704) in the verifier: a bipartite quadrangulation grown from the cube by inserting squares into random faces (minimum degree 3), with a random list of 3 colours from 0..4 per vertex. Each vertex must take a colour from its list and adjacent vertices must differ. The score is the number of properly coloured instances (0..4). Maximize; all are colourable by the Alon-Tarsi theorem. The score counts fixed instances coloured properly from their lists; it measures a constructive list-colouring method for a theorem proved non-constructively. On these four instances a greedy that always colours a vertex with the fewest remaining list colours already reaches the maximum 4 without backtracking.

science-point-sets-without-empty-hexagon.rationale: The candidate returns up to 30 integer points with no three collinear; the evaluator verifies by an exact search that no six of them form an empty convex hexagon and scores the number of points. Reviewed source family science_prize_g_empty_hexagon, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Point sets without an empty convex hexagon (rediscovering 29 points)
evidence.description: construct() -> list of 1..30 distinct integer points [x, y] with |x|, |y| <= 10^6 and no three collinear. No six points may form a convex hexagon with no other point inside (exact search over all convex chains anchored at their lowest vertex). Maximize the number of points; the optimum is 29. Overmars found 29-point sets without empty hexagons and Heule and Scheucher proved every 30-point set has one, so 29 is optimal.

science-powerful-numbers-between-squares.rationale: The candidate returns an integer k up to 10^9; the evaluator counts exactly the powerful numbers strictly between k^2 and (k+1)^2. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_powerful, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Many powerful numbers strictly between consecutive squares (k <= 10^9)
evidence.description: construct() -> an integer k with 1 <= k <= 10^9. The score is the number of powerful integers (p | n implies p^2 | n) strictly between k^2 and (k+1)^2, counted exactly through the unique form a^2 b^3 with b squarefree. Maximize; the optimum is 11. For k <= 10^9 the maximum is 11. Erdős's h(n) counts [n^2, (n+1)^2) and so also includes the square n^2; the task counts the open interval as in OEIS A119241.

science-practical-divisor-sum-5040.rationale: The candidate selects distinct divisors of 5040 that sum to 4979; the evaluator checks divisibility and the sum exactly, and the number of divisors used is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_practical_divisor_sum, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Short sums of distinct divisors of 5040
evidence.description: construct() -> at most 256 distinct positive divisors of n=5040 whose sum is target=4979. Minimize the number of selected divisors. Exact membership and sum checks; this is one finite practical-number instance. Represent 4979 as a sum of distinct divisors of 5040, minimizing the number of terms. This is one finite optimization instance, not Vose’s asymptotic theorem. The optimum is 5, established by an exhaustive search over the 60 divisors; this is a rediscovery task.

science-prime-additive-complement-256.rationale: The candidate constructs a subset B of [0,256] such that every integer in [256,512] is a prime plus an element of B; the evaluator re-derives the primes and checks every target, and the size of B is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_prime_complement, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Small additive complements of the primes
evidence.description: construct() -> a nonempty subset B of [0,n=256] such that every integer in [256,512] is p+b for a prime p and b in B. Minimize |B|. All primes and target coverage are recomputed. Choose B in [0,256] so every integer in [256,512] is prime plus B, and minimize |B|. This only certifies finite coverage, not an asymptotic complement. The optimum is 10, established by an exact set-cover computation; this is a rediscovery task.

science-prime-covers-with-reciprocal-bud.rationale: The candidate chooses residue classes for distinct primes up to 1000 with reciprocal sum at most 1; the evaluator checks the budget in exact rationals and scores the length of the initial interval that is covered. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_budget_cover, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Covering 1..L by prime residue classes with reciprocal budget 1 (primes up to 1000)
evidence.description: construct() -> classes [[p, r], ...] with distinct primes p <= 1000, 0 <= r < p and sum of 1/p at most 1 (exact rationals). The score is the largest L such that every integer 1..L lies in some class (exact, capped at 10^5). Maximize; L >= 999 would realize the Erdős-Ruzsa covering statement at x = 1000 with C = 1. Covered lengths for x = 1000 and C = 1 are finite evidence for the conjecture; reaching 999 would realize it at this size.

science-prime-plus-power-of-two-1e8.rationale: The candidate returns an integer n up to 10^8; the evaluator counts, with deterministic primality tests, the powers of two 2^k for which n - 2^k is prime. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_prime_power_two, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Integers up to 10^8 with many representations n = p + 2^k
evidence.description: construct() -> an integer n with 3 <= n <= 10^8. The score is the number of k >= 0 with n - 2^k prime (deterministic Miller-Rabin). Maximize; the optimum is 19. For n <= 10^8 the maximum is 19, so the task recovers such an integer.

science-primitive-nonempty-subset-sums.rationale: The candidate returns a set of integers in 1..256. The evaluator computes all nonempty subset sums, requires that none divides another and scores the set size. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_733, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large sets with divisibility-incomparable subset sums
evidence.description: construct() -> 1..30 distinct integers in 1..256. Form every NONEMPTY subset sum; no two distinct resulting values may divide one another. Equal sum values are deduplicated (but any repeated subset representation also leads to a forbidden double after cancellation). Maximize set size. The local N=256 construction is checked by exact reachability and a multiples sieve. The empty sum is excluded, and no general asymptotic improvement or formal proof is claimed.

science-projective-blocking-intersection.rationale: The candidate selects points of the projective plane of order seven. The evaluator checks that every line meets the set and scores the largest intersection with a line. Reviewed source family science_prize_d_blocking_set, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Projective blocking sets with small line intersections in PG(2,7)
evidence.description: construct() -> distinct point indices in 0..56 for PG(2,7). Point order is (1,x,y) lexicographically for x,y=0..6, then (0,1,x), then (0,0,1). Every projective line must meet the set. Minimize the maximum intersection with any line; line-contained sets are allowed but score at least 8. The local task searches all point subsets in the prime plane of order seven; it does not constrain candidates to unions of algebraic curves or reproduce that paper's proof. The optimum is 4: an exhaustive search shows that no blocking set meets every line in at most 3 points, so this is a rediscovery task.

science-property-p-divisibility-256.rationale: The candidate constructs a subset of [1,256] in which no element divides the sum of two larger elements (equal summands allowed); the evaluator checks every such triple exactly, and the size of the set is maximized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_property_p, area mathematics.

evidence.description: construct() -> a nonempty subset of [1,n=256]. For every a<b<=c in the set, a must NOT divide b+c. Repeated larger summands b=c are included. Maximize cardinality. Finite cardinality maximization in [1,256], including repeated larger summands. The cited work proves the extremal bound for sufficiently large n; this task claims neither novelty nor its applicability threshold at 256.

science-quantum-ising-vqe.rationale: The candidate chooses parameters of a fixed quantum circuit against simulated expected-cut or ground-state energy objectives; circuit architecture is fixed. Reviewed source family science_vqe_ising, area quantum_information.

evidence.task_name: Quantum information: shallow-circuit Ising ground states
evidence.description: Optimize parameters of a fixed three-layer Ry/CZ circuit to approximate ground states of open transverse-field Ising chains. The evaluator builds each state itself and minimizes the mean energy gap per spin relative to an independent exact eigensolution.

science-quantum-qaoa-maxcut.rationale: The candidate chooses parameters of a fixed quantum circuit against simulated expected-cut or ground-state energy objectives; circuit architecture is fixed. Reviewed source family science_qaoa, area quantum_information.

evidence.task_name: Quantum information: fixed-depth QAOA parameter design
evidence.description: Design graph-dependent two-layer QAOA angles maximizing the mean ratio of the independently simulated expected cut to the exact classical optimum on six small graphs. The circuit architecture is fixed; the candidate controls its parameter-selection algorithm.

science-rainbow-four-cycle-colourings-20.rationale: The candidate constructs an edge-coloured simple graph on 20 vertices with 20 colours; the evaluator enumerates every 4-cycle, requires four distinct colours on each and scores the number of edges. Reviewed source family science_prize_i_rainbow_c4, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Dense graphs on 20 vertices edge-coloured with 20 colours so every 4-cycle is rainbow
evidence.description: construct() -> coloured edges [[u, v, c], ...] of a simple graph on vertices 0..19 with colours 0..19. Every 4-cycle (as a subgraph) must receive four distinct colours, checked over all 4-cycles. Maximize the number of edges. Dense valid colourings for n = 20 are finite evidence on the anti-Ramsey question.

science-ramsey-cube-graph.rationale: The candidate returns a two-colouring of the edges of a complete graph on at most 13 vertices; the evaluator searches each colour class exactly for a copy of the cube graph Q3 and scores the number of vertices. Reviewed source family science_prize_e_cube, area mathematics.

evidence.description: construct() -> {'n': n, 'colors': [...]}: colour 0 or 1 for each pair (i,j), i<j, of vertices 0..n-1 in lexicographic order, 1 <= n <= 13. Neither colour class may contain the 8-vertex cube graph Q3 as a subgraph. Maximize n; the proven optimum is 12. Recovering a 12-vertex colouring with no monochromatic Q3 rediscovers the extremal lower bound.

science-ramsey-five-colour-quadrilateral.rationale: The candidate returns a five-colouring of the edges of a complete graph on at most 29 vertices; the evaluator checks that no colour class has two vertices with two common neighbours (a four-cycle) and scores the number of vertices. Reviewed source family science_prize_e_r5c4, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Five-colourings of complete graphs without monochromatic four-cycles (R_5(K2,2))
evidence.description: construct() -> {'n': n, 'colors': [...]}: one colour in {0,...,4} for each pair (i,j), i<j, of vertices 0..n-1 in lexicographic order, 1 <= n <= 29. No colour class may contain a four-cycle (no two vertices with two common neighbours in one colour). Maximize n. A valid 5-colouring of K_n certifies R_5(C4) > n. The algebraic construction of Lazebnik and Woldar gives 26 vertices; 27 or 28 would be new.

science-ramsey-four-clique-versus-indepe.rationale: The candidate returns a graph on at most 25 vertices; the evaluator checks by exact search that it has no K4 and no independent set of five vertices and scores the number of vertices. Reviewed source family science_prize_e_ramsey_4_5, area mathematics.

evidence.description: construct() -> {'n': n, 'edges': [[u, v], ...]}: a simple graph on vertices 0..n-1 with 1 <= n <= 25. It must contain no K4 and no independent set of 5 vertices, checked exactly. Maximize n; the proven optimum is 24. Finding a 24-vertex (4,5)-graph recovers Kalbfleisch's lower bound; no 25-vertex graph exists.

science-ramsey-four-clique-versus-indepe.rationale: The candidate returns a graph on at most 40 vertices; the evaluator checks by exact search that it has no K4 and no independent set of six vertices and scores the number of vertices. Reviewed source family science_prize_e_ramsey_4_6, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: K4-free graphs without independent 6-sets (Ramsey number R(4,6))
evidence.description: construct() -> {'n': n, 'edges': [[u, v], ...]}: a simple graph on vertices 0..n-1 with 1 <= n <= 40. It must contain no K4 and no independent set of 6 vertices, checked exactly. Maximize n. A valid graph on n vertices certifies R(4,6) > n. Exoo's 35-vertex graph is the published record; 36 vertices would be a new lower bound.

science-ramsey-four-colour-hexagon.rationale: The candidate returns a four-colouring of the edges of a complete graph on at most 20 vertices; the evaluator searches each colour class exactly for a six-cycle and scores the number of vertices. Reviewed source family science_prize_e_r4c6, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Four-colourings of complete graphs without monochromatic hexagons (R_4(C6))
evidence.description: construct() -> {'n': n, 'colors': [...]}: one colour in {0,1,2,3} for each pair (i,j), i<j, of vertices 0..n-1 in lexicographic order, 1 <= n <= 20. No colour class may contain a six-cycle (exact search for not necessarily induced cycles). Maximize n. A valid 4-colouring of K_n certifies R_4(C6) > n. The best known colouring has 17 vertices; 18 or 19 vertices would be new.

science-ramsey-four-colour-triangle.rationale: The candidate returns a four-colouring of the edges of a complete graph on at most 62 vertices; the evaluator checks that no colour class contains a triangle and scores the number of vertices. Reviewed source family science_prize_e_r3333, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Four-colourings of complete graphs without monochromatic triangles (R(3,3,3,3))
evidence.description: construct() -> {'n': n, 'colors': [...]}: one colour in {0,1,2,3} for each pair (i,j), i<j, of vertices 0..n-1 in lexicographic order, 1 <= n <= 62. No colour class may contain a triangle. Maximize n. A valid 4-colouring of K_n certifies R_4(3) > n. Chung's 50-vertex colouring is the record; 51 vertices would be new.

science-ramsey-four-cycle-versus-indepen.rationale: The candidate returns a graph on at most 43 vertices; the evaluator checks that it has no four-cycle and, by exact search, no independent set of eleven vertices, and scores the number of vertices. Reviewed source family science_prize_e_c4_versus_k11, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Four-cycle-free graphs without independent 11-sets (Ramsey number R(C4,K11))
evidence.description: construct() -> {'n': n, 'edges': [[u, v], ...]}: a simple graph on vertices 0..n-1 with 1 <= n <= 43. No two vertices may have two common neighbours (no C4), and there must be no independent set of 11 vertices (exact search). Maximize n. A valid graph on n vertices certifies R(C4,K11) > n. The best known construction has 39 vertices.

science-ramsey-four-cycle-versus-star-39.rationale: The candidate returns a graph on at most 47 vertices; the evaluator checks that it has no four-cycle and minimum degree at least n-39 (so the complement has no star K1,39) and scores the number of vertices. Reviewed source family science_prize_e_c4_versus_star39, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Four-cycle-free graphs of large minimum degree (Ramsey number R(C4,K1,39))
evidence.description: construct() -> {'n': n, 'edges': [[u, v], ...]}: a simple graph on vertices 0..n-1 with 1 <= n <= 47, containing no C4, whose minimum degree is at least n - 39 (so the complement has no K1,39). Maximize n. A C4-free graph on n vertices with minimum degree at least n-39 certifies R(C4,K1,39) > n. The value is known to be 46 or 47, so 46 vertices would settle it.

science-ramsey-induced-degree-diversity.rationale: The candidate selects at least eight vertices of the Paley graph on 17 vertices. The evaluator counts the distinct degrees in the induced subgraph. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_518, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Many distinct induced degrees in a Ramsey host
evidence.description: construct() -> distinct vertices of the pinned 17-vertex graph, selecting at least eight. Maximize the number of distinct vertex degrees in the induced subgraph. The evaluator checks that the host has no clique or independent set of size four. The input is the classical Paley graph of order 17, and at least eight vertices must be retained. The published theorem concerns growing hosts and unspecified constants; no asymptotic or optimality claim follows from this instance.

science-ramsey-octahedron.rationale: The candidate returns a two-colouring of the edges of a complete graph on at most 31 vertices; the evaluator searches each colour class exactly for the octahedron K2,2,2 and scores the number of vertices. Reviewed source family science_prize_e_octahedron, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Two-colourings without a monochromatic octahedron K2,2,2 (R(K2,2,2))
evidence.description: construct() -> {'n': n, 'colors': [...]}: colour 0 or 1 for each pair (i,j), i<j, of vertices 0..n-1 in lexicographic order, 1 <= n <= 31. Neither colour class may contain K2,2,2 as a (not necessarily induced) subgraph. Maximize n. A valid colouring of K_n certifies R(K2,2,2) > n. The record has 29 vertices; a 30-vertex colouring would prove R(K2,2,2) = 31.

science-ramsey-pentagon-versus-independe.rationale: The candidate constructs a simple graph on at most 35 vertices; the evaluator searches exhaustively for a 5-cycle and for an independent set of nine vertices, rejects the graph if either exists and scores the number of vertices. Reviewed source family science_prize_i_c5_versus_k9, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Pentagon-free graphs without independent 9-sets (Ramsey number R(C5,K9))
evidence.description: construct() -> {'n': n, 'edges': [[u, v], ...]}: a simple graph on vertices 0..n-1 with 1 <= n <= 35 containing no 5-cycle (as a subgraph) and no independent set of 9 vertices, both checked exactly. Maximize n. A valid graph on n vertices certifies R(C5,K9) > n; the best known has 32 vertices and no valid graph has more than 35.

science-ramsey-triangle-versus-independe.rationale: The candidate returns a graph on at most 41 vertices; the evaluator checks by exact search that it has no triangle and no independent set of ten vertices and scores the number of vertices. Reviewed source family science_prize_e_ramsey_3_10, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Triangle-free graphs without independent 10-sets (Ramsey number R(3,10))
evidence.description: construct() -> {'n': n, 'edges': [[u, v], ...]}: a simple graph on vertices 0..n-1 with 1 <= n <= 41. It must contain no triangle and no independent set of 10 vertices; both conditions are checked by exact branch and bound. Maximize n. A valid graph on n vertices certifies R(3,10) > n. The survey records 39 as the largest known order, and R(3,10) <= 41 limits any valid graph to 40 vertices.

science-ramsey-two-triangles-versus-four.rationale: The candidate returns a three-colouring of the edges of a complete graph on at most 30 vertices; the evaluator checks that two colours are triangle-free and the third is K4-free and scores the number of vertices. Reviewed source family science_prize_e_r334, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Three-colourings avoiding two triangle colours and a K4 (rediscovering R(3,3,4) = 30)
evidence.description: construct() -> {'n': n, 'colors': [...]}: one colour in {0,1,2} for each pair (i,j), i<j, of vertices 0..n-1 in lexicographic order, 1 <= n <= 30. Colours 0 and 1 must be triangle-free and colour 2 must be K4-free. Maximize n; the proven optimum is 29. A valid colouring of K_n certifies R(3,3,4) > n; the optimum is 29 vertices.

science-random-graph-biclique-partition.rationale: The candidate partitions the edges of a fixed 30-vertex graph into complete bipartite subgraphs. The evaluator checks that every edge is covered exactly once and counts the parts. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_664, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Small exact biclique partitions of a random graph
evidence.description: construct() -> list of bicliques, each [left_vertices,right_vertices] with nonempty disjoint sides. Every cross pair must be a host edge. The cross-edge sets must partition all pinned graph edges exactly once. Within-side edges are allowed. Minimize number of bicliques. One local G(30,1/2) sample (random.Random(664)) is pinned. The star baseline is independently encoded; scores are partition upper bounds on this finite sample, not typical asymptotic minima.

science-random-graph-hamiltonian-arrival.rationale: The candidate returns a Hamilton cycle on 24 vertices. The evaluator scores the latest position of its edges in a fixed random ordering of all edges. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_614, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Hamilton cycles appearing early in an edge process
evidence.description: construct() -> a permutation of vertices 0..23, describing a Hamilton cycle with implicit closing edge. Score is the largest one-based arrival index of its edges in the pinned uniformly shuffled complete-graph edge list. Minimize that prefix index. The evaluator certifies presence, not absence of all earlier Hamilton cycles. One complete-edge permutation on 24 vertices, locally shuffled with random.Random(614), replaces an asymptotic random ensemble. Each score is an upper bound on this sample’s true hitting time, not proof that it is earliest.

science-random-hypergraph-matching-arriv.rationale: The candidate returns a perfect matching of six triples on 18 vertices. The evaluator scores the latest position of its triples in a fixed random ordering of all triples. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_615, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Perfect matchings appearing early in a triple process
evidence.description: construct() -> six disjoint triples covering vertices 0..17 exactly once. Score is the largest one-based arrival index of the six triples in the pinned shuffled list of all triples. Minimize this prefix index. No claimed earliest index is trusted. The task uses one locally shuffled three-uniform process on 18 vertices (random.Random(615)). It produces a certified prefix upper bound, not an asymptotic threshold or an exact earliest-prefix proof.

science-rough-numbers-in-consecutive-pri.rationale: For each of 32 fixed gaps between consecutive primes the candidate may give an interior integer whose least prime factor is at least the gap length. The evaluator verifies each witness and counts the certified gaps. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_554, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Rough integer witnesses inside consecutive prime gaps
evidence.description: construct() -> a list aligned with the 32 pinned consecutive-prime pairs. Each entry is either None (no certificate) or an integer STRICTLY between its pair whose least prime factor is at least the prime gap. Supply at least one witness; maximize certified gaps. The verifier checks primality, consecutiveness and every least factor independently. None never asserts nonexistence. Thirty-two consecutive gaps beginning at 10007 are pinned. Some gaps may have no witness and a skipped gap does not prove that. This finite certificate count does not imply a universal all-gap result or the paper’s density estimate.

science-runs-with-large-prime-factors.rationale: The candidate names a run of consecutive integers starting at most at 10^4; the evaluator factors each term, checks that it has a prime factor larger than the run length and scores the length. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_large_factor_run, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Runs of consecutive integers each with a prime factor larger than the run length (start at most 10^4)
evidence.description: construct() -> {'start': s, 'length': k} with 1 <= s <= 10^4 and 1 <= k <= 200. Each of s, ..., s + k - 1 must have a prime factor greater than k (exact factorization). Maximize k; the optimum is 30. For runs starting at most 10^4 the maximum is 30, so the task recovers such a run.

science-short-square-product-extension.rationale: The candidate returns integers above 210 whose product with 210 is a perfect square. The evaluator checks the square exactly and scores how far the largest integer lies above 210. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_697, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Short intervals supplying a square-product extension
evidence.description: construct() -> 1..100 distinct integers strictly larger than 210 and at most 10210. Their product multiplied by 210 must be a perfect square. Minimize max(selected integers)-210. An arbitrary-precision integer square root verifies the exact condition. The task fixes n=210, a nonsquare, and bounds the certificate and following window. A certificate gives an upper bound on t_210, whose value under the local convention is 28 (a(210) = 238 in OEIS A006255); the distribution over n is not established.

science-sidon-extension-of-1-2-5-11.rationale: The candidate returns a set in [1, 284] that contains 1, 2, 5 and 11; the evaluator checks that all pairwise sums are distinct and scores the size. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_sidon_extension, area mathematics.

evidence.description: construct() -> distinct integers in 1..284 containing 1, 2, 5 and 11 whose pairwise sums a + b (a <= b) are all distinct. Maximize the size; without the prescribed elements the maximum in [1, 284] is 20 (the optimal 20-mark Golomb ruler has length 283). Scores near 20 would show that the prescribed elements barely reduce the attainable size at this scale; no value for this seed is documented.

science-sidon-prefix-of-perfect-differen.rationale: The candidate returns up to 32 integers including 0 whose positive differences are all distinct and include 1..30; the evaluator checks both conditions exactly and scores the largest element. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_unique_differences, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Sidon sets containing 0 whose differences include 1, ..., 30 (prefixes of perfect difference sets)
evidence.description: construct() -> at most 32 distinct integers in 0..10^6 including 0, with all positive differences distinct (a Sidon set) and every d in 1..30 occurring as a difference. Minimize the largest element. A Sidon set realizing all differences 1..30 is a truncated perfect difference set; its least possible diameter measures the growth cost at this scale.

science-sidon-sets-of-squares-68.rationale: The candidate selects bases among 1..68; the evaluator checks that all sums of two of their squares are distinct and scores the number of bases. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_sidon_squares, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Largest Sidon set among the first 68 squares
evidence.description: construct() -> distinct bases x in 1..68 whose squares form a Sidon set: all sums x^2 + y^2 with x <= y are distinct. Maximize the number of bases; the optimum is 32. For N = 68 the maximum is 32, so the task recovers an extremal set.
