science-small-books-above-turan-40.rationale: The candidate returns exactly 401 edges on 40 vertices; the evaluator computes the largest number of triangles sharing one edge (the largest book), and smaller is better. Reviewed source family science_prize_f_books, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Graphs with 40 vertices and 401 edges whose largest book is small
evidence.description: construct() -> exactly 401 distinct edges [u, v] on vertices 0..39. The score is the largest book: the maximum over edges of the number of triangles containing that edge. Minimize; the theorem of Edwards and Khadzhiivanov-Nikiforov gives score >= 40/6. For n = 40 and one edge above n^2/4 the theorem gives a book of size at least 7; the least achievable value for this finite size is not documented.

science-small-prime-primitive-roots.rationale: For each of twelve fixed prime moduli the candidate gives a prime primitive root. The evaluator verifies primality and multiplicative order and scores the sum of the roots. Reviewed source family science_prize_d_prime_primitive_roots, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Small prime primitive roots for twelve prime moduli
evidence.description: construct() -> twelve Python prime integers, one for each modulus [101,103,107,109,113,127,131,137,139,149,151,157]. Each root is at most 100000, coprime to its modulus, and has multiplicative order p-1. Minimize the sum of these prime roots. Twelve small fixed moduli provide a finite construction/rediscovery instance; exact orders are verified without reproducing the shifted sieve.

science-smallest-triangle-free-five-chro.rationale: The candidate returns a graph on at most 23 vertices; the evaluator checks that it is triangle-free and, by exact backtracking, not 4-colourable, and scores the number of vertices, fewer being better. Reviewed source family science_prize_e_triangle_free_five_chromatic, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Smallest triangle-free graph of chromatic number five (rediscovering 22 vertices)
evidence.description: construct() -> {'n': n, 'edges': [[u, v], ...]}: a simple triangle-free graph on vertices 0..n-1 with 1 <= n <= 23 that is not 4-colourable (exact backtracking). Minimize n; the proven optimum is 22. Any valid graph certifies h_3(5) <= n; the optimum 22 was established by exhaustive computer search.

science-smooth-divisibility-antichain-su.rationale: The candidate writes each integer from 1 to 128 as a sum of distinct numbers of the form 2^a 3^b 5^c, none dividing another; the evaluator verifies every representation exactly, and the total number of summands is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_antichain_representations, area mathematics.

evidence.description: construct() -> 128 rows corresponding to targets 1..128. Every row must contain 1..30 distinct positive 2^a*3^b*5^c terms summing to its target; no chosen term may divide another. All targets require valid representations. Minimize the total number of summands over all targets, an explicit local refinement of finite d-completeness. Represent targets 1..128 by sums of distinct 2,3,5-smooth numbers forming a divisibility antichain. All targets require valid representations; minimizing the total term count is an explicit local efficiency refinement of finite d-completeness. The seed uses up to three terms and is not term-minimal.

science-smooth-runs-after-prime-squares.rationale: The candidate returns a prime p up to 10^9 and a length k; the evaluator factors p^2+1, ..., p^2+k exactly, checks that no prime factor exceeds p and scores k. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_smooth_square, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Long runs after p^2 with no prime factor exceeding p (p <= 10^9)
evidence.description: construct() -> {'p': p, 'k': k} with p a prime at most 10^9 and 1 <= k <= 200; every integer p^2 + 1, ..., p^2 + k must have all prime factors at most p (exact factorization by trial division and Pollard-Brent with deterministic Miller-Rabin). Maximize k. Long runs for p <= 10^9 are finite evidence for the conjectured positive answer.

science-software-ci-prioritization-iofro.rationale: The candidate orders the tests of each continuous-integration cycle of an industrial log using only the verdicts of earlier cycles; the evaluator reveals a cycle's verdicts after its order is committed and scores the mean APFD. Reviewed source family science_software_ci_prioritization, area software_engineering.

evidence.task_name: Software engineering: history-based test prioritisation in continuous integration (ABB IOF/ROL)
evidence.description: Order the test cases of each of the 320 continuous-integration cycles of ABB's IOF/ROL system so that failing tests run early, using only the verdicts of earlier cycles. Each cycle's verdicts are revealed after its order is committed; the score is the mean APFD over cycles with both failing and passing tests.

science-software-ci-prioritization-paint.rationale: The candidate orders the tests of each continuous-integration cycle of an industrial log using only the verdicts of earlier cycles; the evaluator reveals a cycle's verdicts after its order is committed and scores the mean APFD. evidence.description: Order the test cases of each of the 352 continuous-integration cycles of ABB's Paint Control system so that failing tests run early, using only the verdicts of earlier cycles. science-software-cit-apache-2way.rationale: The candidate generates a covering array for a configurable-software model under its forbidden combinations; the evaluator rejects rows with a forbidden combination, checks that every feasible t-way combination is covered and scores the number of rows. evidence.description: Build a smallest pairwise covering array for the 172-option Apache web-server model of Cohen et al., avoiding its forbidden option combinations. Every feasible pair of option settings must appear in some test configuration; fewer configurations is better.

evidence.description: Build a smallest pairwise covering array for the 35-parameter Healthcare4 model, one of the IBM industrial combinatorial test design models of Segall et al., under its forbidden value combinations. Every feasible pair of values must appear in some test; fewer tests is better.

evidence.description: Build a smallest pairwise covering array for the 55-option SPIN model-checker verifier model under the archive's 1434 forbidden option pairs. Every feasible pair of option settings must appear in some test configuration; fewer configurations is better.

science-software-coalescing-large.rationale: The candidate colours register-interference graphs of the Appel-George coalescing challenge with a fixed number of registers; the evaluator checks precolouring and every interference edge and scores the share of move weight left uncoalesced. evidence.task_name: Software engineering: optimal register coalescing on the 22 largest challenge graphs
evidence.description: Colour the 22 interference graphs with 3,000 to 28,640 nodes from the Appel-George Optimal Coalescing Challenge with 6 registers so that as much move (affinity) weight as possible joins nodes of the same colour. The score is the mean share of affinity weight left uncoalesced; lower is better.

science-software-coalescing-small.rationale: The candidate colours register-interference graphs of the Appel-George coalescing challenge with a fixed number of registers; the evaluator checks precolouring and every interference edge and scores the share of move weight left uncoalesced. Reviewed source family science_software_coalescing, area systems_and_hardware.

evidence.task_name: Software engineering: optimal register coalescing on the challenge graphs with fewer than 3,000 nodes
evidence.description: Colour the 452 smaller interference graphs of the Appel-George Optimal Coalescing Challenge with 6 registers so that as much move (affinity) weight as possible joins nodes of the same colour. The score is the mean share of affinity weight left uncoalesced; lower is better.

science-software-fault-localization-seed.rationale: The candidate maps a program spectrum (per block, counts of failing and passing tests that execute it) to suspiciousness scores; the evaluator ranks the blocks of 532 seeded faults in three CPython modules and scores the mean relative rank (EXAM) of the faulty block. Reviewed source family science_software_fault_localization, area software_engineering.

evidence.task_name: Software engineering: spectrum-based fault localisation of seeded faults in three CPython modules
evidence.description: Rank the code blocks of a faulty module by suspiciousness using only its program spectrum: for each block, how many failing and passing tests execute it. The 532 faults are first-order mutants of textwrap, urllib.parse and fractions; the score is the mean EXAM (rank of the faulty block divided by the number of blocks).

science-software-fuzz-htmlparser.rationale: The candidate generates a bounded number of input strings for one CPython standard-library parser; the evaluator replays them on source instrumented with its own block probes and scores the number of distinct probes reached. science-software-log-parsing-loghub2k.rationale: The candidate groups the 2,000 messages of each of 16 system logs by the log statement that produced them, from the message texts alone; the evaluator scores the mean grouping accuracy against the corrected Loghub-2k event labels, which stay in the evaluator process. Reviewed source family science_software_log_parsing, area software_engineering.

evidence.task_name: Software engineering: log parsing (event template identification) on the 16 Loghub-2k data sets
evidence.description: Group the messages of 16 system logs (2,000 lines each, from HDFS, Hadoop, Spark, Linux, OpenSSH and others) by the log statement that produced them, given only the message texts. The score is the mean grouping accuracy against the corrected ground-truth events.

science-software-loop-invariants-code2in.rationale: The candidate proposes a linear-integer loop invariant for each Code2Inv program, with a budgeted counterexample oracle; the evaluator parses each term against a whitelist and scores the fraction of programs for which Z3 proves initiation, consecution and the post-condition. evidence.task_name: Software engineering: loop-invariant inference for the Code2Inv programs
evidence.description: Infer a loop invariant for each of the 124 valid Code2Inv C programs so that Z3 proves initiation, consecution and the post-condition. science-software-mutation-fractions.rationale: The candidate generates a bounded number of test calls for one CPython standard-library module after seeing its source and first-order mutants; the evaluator replays the calls on the original and on every mutant and scores the fraction of mutants whose outcome differs. science-software-quixbugs-repair.rationale: The candidate is a repair procedure that receives a buggy QuixBugs Python program with visible tests and returns a patched program within a two-statement edit bound; the evaluator runs visible, held-out and generated tests and scores the fraction of programs whose patch passes all of them. science-software-superoptimization-hacke.rationale: The candidate rewrites each of 25 Hacker's Delight bit-manipulation kernels as a shorter straight-line 32-bit program; the evaluator tests each program on 300 inputs, asks Z3 to prove equivalence with the reference and scores the total instruction count, counting unproven programs at the reference length. science-sparse-random-graph-long-path.rationale: The candidate returns a simple path in a fixed sparse 100-vertex graph. The evaluator checks that every step is an edge and scores the number of vertices on the path. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_748, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Long paths above the random-graph phase transition
evidence.description: construct() -> a nonempty ordered list of distinct vertices in 0..99 forming a simple path in the pinned graph; all consecutive pairs must be edges. Maximize path vertex count. No path-closing edge is required. A locally generated G(100,1.8/100) sample, using random.Random(748), is pinned. The finite path score certifies a lower bound for this one graph, without proving a high-probability asymptotic result.

science-sparse-ruler-200.rationale: The candidate returns integer marks in 0..200; the evaluator checks that every distance 1..200 is a difference of two marks and scores the number of marks. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_sparse_ruler, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Sparse ruler of length 200 with the fewest marks
evidence.description: construct() -> distinct integer marks in 0..200 such that every distance 1..200 is a difference of two marks. Minimize the number of marks; the optimum is 25. For N = 200 the minimum is 25, so the task recovers an optimal ruler.

science-square-products-condition-200.rationale: The candidate returns a subset of {1..200}; the evaluator finds every four elements with a square product through parity vectors of prime exponents, checks the condition ad = bc and scores the size. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_square_products, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Subsets of {1, ..., 200} in which square products of four elements force ad = bc
evidence.description: construct() -> distinct integers in 1..200 such that whenever a <= b <= c <= d are elements (repetition allowed) with abcd a perfect square, ad = bc (checked exactly through parity vectors of prime exponents). Maximize the size; the optimum is 102. For n = 200 the maximum is 102, so the task recovers an extremal set.

science-squarefree-pairwise-sums-512.rationale: The candidate returns a subset of {1..512}; the evaluator checks that every sum of two elements is squarefree and scores the size. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_squarefree_sums, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large subsets of {1, ..., 512} whose pairwise sums are all squarefree
evidence.description: construct() -> distinct integers in 1..512 such that every sum a + b with a <= b (including 2a) is squarefree. Maximize the size; the optimum is 24. For N = 512 the maximum is 24, so the task recovers an extremal set. The bank entry is the infinite question (#1103); this is its finite analogue (#1109).

science-steiner-system-s5612-packing.rationale: The candidate returns distinct 6-subsets of 12 points; the evaluator checks that no 5-subset lies in two blocks and scores the number of blocks. Reviewed source family science_prize_f_witt_design, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Packings of 6-sets on 12 points with no repeated 5-subset (the Witt design S(5,6,12))
evidence.description: construct() -> list of distinct 6-subsets of 0..11 such that no 5-subset lies in two blocks. Maximize the number of blocks; the optimum 132 is attained exactly by the Steiner system S(5,6,12). Each block covers six 5-subsets of the 792, so at most 132 blocks fit; 132 is attained only by the Witt design S(5,6,12).

science-strong-edge-colouring-instances.rationale: The candidate returns an edge colouring for each of three fixed seeded bounded-degree graphs; the evaluator regenerates the graphs, checks that every colour class is an induced matching and scores the total number of colours used. Reviewed source family science_prize_i_strong_edge_colouring, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Strong edge colourings of three fixed bounded-degree graphs
evidence.description: construct() -> three lists of edge colours, one per instance from bounded_degree_graph(n, d, seed) for (40,4,101), (60,5,102), (80,6,103) in the verifier; colours are integers in 0..m-1, where m is the number of edges of the instance, and follow the sorted edge order. Each colour class must be an induced matching (no two edges share a vertex or are joined by an edge). Minimize the total number of colours used; the Erdős-Nešetřil conjecture predicts at most 5d^2/4 colours for even d and (5d^2 - 2d + 1)/4 for odd d per instance (20 + 29 + 45). The score totals colours on three fixed graphs of maximum degree 4, 5 and 6; it measures a colouring method, not the conjecture.

science-sum-free-subsets-instances.rationale: The candidate returns a subset of each of three fixed seeded sets of nonzero integers; the evaluator regenerates the sets, checks that no a + b = c holds inside each subset and scores the total size. Reviewed source family science_prize_i_sum_free_subsets, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large sum-free subsets of three fixed sets of integers
evidence.description: construct() -> three subsets, one per instance from sum_free_instance(size, seed) for (60,801), (120,802), (240,803) in the verifier (distinct nonzero integers in [-10000, 10000]). Each subset must be sum-free: no a + b = c with a, b, c in it (a = b allowed). Maximize the total size; every n-element set has a sum-free subset of size at least (n+2)/3 (Bourgain). The score totals sum-free subset sizes on three fixed random sets; it measures a search method, not the worst case in f(n). The exact optimum is 328 (55 + 103 + 170), which integer programming on the triples a + b = c finds in seconds.

science-sums-of-three-prime-cubes-1e10.rationale: The candidate returns an integer N up to 10^10 with a list of prime triples; the evaluator checks that the cubes of each triple sum to N and scores the number of distinct triples. evidence.task_name: Integers up to 10^10 with many representations as sums of three prime cubes
evidence.description: construct() -> {'N': N, 'triples': [[p, q, r], ...]} with N <= 10^10 and distinct prime triples p <= q <= r (each at most 3000) with p^3 + q^3 + r^3 = N. Maximize the number of triples; the optimum is 4. For k = 3 and N <= 10^10 the maximum is 4, so the task recovers such an N.

science-sums-of-two-cubes-many-ways.rationale: The candidate returns an integer m with a list of pairs of positive integers; the evaluator checks a^3 + b^3 = m for each pair and scores the number of distinct pairs. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_taxicab, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Integers up to 5*10^16 with many representations as sums of two positive cubes
evidence.description: construct() -> {'m': m, 'pairs': [[a, b], ...]} with 2 <= m <= 5*10^16 and distinct pairs of positive integers a <= b with a^3 + b^3 = m (checked exactly). Maximize the number of pairs; the optimum is 5, attained by a single integer in this range. Below 5*10^16 the maximum is 5 and a single integer attains it, so the task is a calibrated rediscovery.

science-sums-of-two-powerful-numbers.rationale: The candidate returns an integer N up to 10^18 with a list of pairs of powerful numbers that sum to N; the evaluator verifies every pair by exact factorization and scores the number of distinct pairs. Reviewed source family science_prize_i_powerful_pairs, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Integers up to 10^18 with many representations as sums of two powerful numbers
evidence.description: construct() -> {'N': N, 'pairs': [[a, b], ...]} with 2 <= N <= 10^18 and between 1 and 1000 distinct pairs a <= b, a + b = N (a list of more than 1000 pairs is rejected, so the score is at most 1000), where a and b are powerful (every prime factor appears squared; 1 counts as powerful), checked by exact factorization. The score is the number of pairs, a certified lower bound on the representation count. Maximize. The cap of 1000 listed pairs is attainable: integers below 10^18 with more than 1000 representations as a sum of two squares exist, and squares are powerful. So 1000 is the maximum score and the task is a capped search exercise, not evidence on the conjectured subpolynomial bound.

This is a finite construction adaptation of JSP-000022; a finite high score cannot prove the universal Černý conjecture.

science-three-chromatic-triple-system.rationale: The candidate returns a system of triples on nine vertices together with a proper three-colouring. The evaluator checks the colouring, rules out every two-colouring exhaustively and scores the number of triples. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_688, area mathematics.

evidence.description: construct() -> {'edges': distinct triples on 0..8, 'colors': nine labels from 0..2}. Every edge must be nonmonochromatic in the provided coloring. The evaluator exhaustively rejects any hypergraph admitting a two-coloring. Minimize edge count among exactly three-chromatic triple systems. This is a rediscovery task: the literature states the optimum f(3,3)=7, attainable within nine vertices. The ten-edge complete-triple-system baseline can improve to that known optimum; no mathematical novelty is asserted.

science-three-colors-every-four-progress.rationale: The candidate colors the integers 1 to 128 so that every four-term arithmetic progression carries at least three colors; the evaluator checks every progression exactly, and the number of colors used is minimized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_three_color_progressions, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Colorings with three colors in every four-term progression
evidence.description: construct() -> n=128 integer color labels in 0..127. Every nonconstant four-term progression of positions must use AT LEAST three distinct colors. Minimize the number of labels actually used; labels need not be consecutive. Minimize colors on [1,128] with at least three colors on every four-term progression. The source’s largest forcing-color threshold is one below the least avoiding-color count; local score uses the latter convention.

science-three-progression-differences-32.rationale: The candidate returns 32 distinct integers in 1..512; the evaluator counts the distinct common differences of three-term arithmetic progressions contained in the set. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_ap_differences, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Thirty-two integers with many distinct 3-term progression differences
evidence.description: construct() -> exactly 32 distinct integers in 1..512. The score is the number of distinct d > 0 such that a, a + d, a + 2d all lie in the set for some a. Maximize. A 32-element set with many progression differences is a finite construction for this extremal function.

science-three-sunflower-free-four-sets-1.rationale: The candidate constructs a family of four-element subsets of a 16-element set containing no three sets whose pairwise intersections coincide; the evaluator checks every triple of sets exactly, and the family size is maximized. Reviewed source family science_prize_a_sunflower_free, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large four-uniform families without three sunflowers
evidence.description: construct() -> 1..maximum=250 distinct k=4 element subsets of [1,n=16]. No three distinct sets may have all three pairwise intersections equal, including an empty common core. Maximize family cardinality. Maximize a family of four-element subsets of [1,16], with at most 250 members, excluding three-petal sunflowers including the empty-core case.

science-totient-value-with-1000-preimage.rationale: The candidate returns an integer m up to 10^8; the evaluator counts the solutions of phi(x) = m exactly, requires exactly 1000 of them and scores m. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_totient, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Smallest totient value with exactly 1000 preimages
evidence.description: construct() -> an integer m with 1 <= m <= 10^8 such that phi(x) = m has exactly 1000 solutions x (counted exactly by recursion over the primes p with p - 1 dividing m). Minimize m. The least value with exactly 1000 preimages is tabulated (it is the reference in state_of_the_art); it is not printed here because the value is itself the answer.

science-tournament-four-dominated.rationale: The candidate returns a tournament on 5 to 90 vertices; the evaluator checks every set of four vertices for a common dominating vertex and scores the number of vertices, fewer being better. Reviewed source family science_prize_e_schutte, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Small tournaments in which every four vertices have a common dominator (Schütte's problem, k = 4)
evidence.description: construct() -> {'n': n, 'orientation': [...]}: one bit per pair (i,j), i<j, of vertices 0..n-1 in lexicographic order (0 means i -> j, 1 means j -> i), 5 <= n <= 90. Every set of 4 vertices must have a vertex with arcs to all four. Minimize n. A valid tournament on n vertices certifies f(4) <= n. The smallest known has 67 vertices; the lower bound f(k) >= (k+2) 2^(k-1) - 1 of Szekeres and Szekeres gives f(4) >= 47.

science-transitive-subtournament-minimum.rationale: The candidate orients the edges of a tournament on 20 vertices. The evaluator computes the size of its largest transitive subtournament exactly. Reviewed source family science_prize_d_transitive_tournament, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Tournaments with small largest transitive subtournaments
evidence.description: construct() -> 190 integer bits, one for each pair (i,j), i<j, in lexicographic order on 20 vertices. Bit 0 orients i to j and bit 1 orients j to i. Minimize the exact largest transitive induced subtournament, computed by source-vertex subset recursion. The local n=20 task minimizes the largest transitive subset rather than reproducing the larger R(7) computation. This small order is labelled rediscovery, with no new-bound claim.

science-tree-packing-20.rationale: The candidate returns injective vertex maps placing fixed generated trees on 1 to 20 vertices into the complete graph K20; the evaluator checks that the embedded trees share no edge and scores the number of packed edges. Reviewed source family science_prize_f_tree_packing, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Packing trees T1..T20 into K20 (Gyárfás tree packing conjecture)
evidence.description: construct() -> 20 entries; entry k-1 is None or an injective list of host vertices in 0..19 for the fixed tree T_k on k vertices (Prüfer-sequence trees from instance_trees(20, 611) in the verifier). Embedded trees must be edge-disjoint in K20. Maximize the number of packed edges; a complete packing uses all 190 edges. The conjecture predicts a perfect packing (190 edges) for this fixed tree sequence; scores measure packing search on one instance.

science-triangle-degree-sums-above-turan.rationale: The candidate constructs a simple graph on 16 vertices with exactly 65 edges; the evaluator enumerates all triangles and scores the largest sum of the three vertex degrees. Reviewed source family science_prize_i_triangle_degrees, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Graphs on 16 vertices with 65 edges whose triangles have small degree sums
evidence.description: construct() -> {'n': 16, 'edges': [[u, v], ...]}: a simple graph on 16 vertices with exactly 65 = floor(16^2/4) + 1 edges (so it has triangles). The score is the largest degree sum deg(u) + deg(v) + deg(w) over its triangles. Minimize. Scores below 24 would beat the published construction at n = 16; the best asymptotic construction gives about 1.4639n = 23.4 (a note of July 2026, not yet published in a journal, reports a disproof of the Bollobás-Erdős conjecture h(n) >= (2(sqrt 3 - 1) - o(1))n by a blow-up of the butterfly graph).

science-triangle-free-bipartization-23.rationale: The candidate returns the edge list of a triangle-free graph on 23 vertices; the evaluator computes the maximum cut over all bipartitions and scores the number of edges outside it (the deletions needed to make the graph bipartite). Reviewed source family science_prize_f_bipartization, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Triangle-free graphs on 23 vertices that are far from bipartite
evidence.description: construct() -> list of edges [u, v] of a simple triangle-free graph on vertices 0..22. The score is the least number of edges whose deletion leaves a bipartite graph, computed exactly as edges minus the maximum cut over all 2^22 bipartitions. Maximize; the known optimum is 20. The finite maximum over triangle-free graphs on 23 vertices is 20 (below the conjectured bound 21.16); recovering it tests constructions near the extremal C5 blow-ups.

science-triangle-free-dense-halves-20.rationale: The candidate returns the edge list of a triangle-free graph on 20 vertices; the evaluator computes the minimum number of edges induced by any ten vertices over all subsets, and larger is better. Reviewed source family science_prize_f_sparse_halves, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Triangle-free graphs on 20 vertices whose every half is dense
evidence.description: construct() -> list of edges [u, v] of a simple triangle-free graph on vertices 0..19. The score is the minimum number of edges induced by any 10 of the vertices, computed over all 184756 subsets. Maximize; a score above 8 would disprove the Erdős-Rousseau conjecture for n = 20. For n = 20 the conjectured maximum of the score is 8, and triangle-free graphs with score 8 are known; a triangle-free graph with score 9 would be a counterexample.

science-triangle-free-diameter-augmentat.rationale: The candidate adds edges to a fixed 24-vertex path. The evaluator checks that the result is triangle-free with diameter at most four and scores the number of added edges. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_501, area mathematics.

evidence.description: construct() -> list of added undirected edges [u,v] on vertices 0..23. Existing edges and duplicate edges are forbidden. The union with the pinned path must remain triangle-free, connected and have diameter at most four. Minimize the number of added edges. The host is a locally chosen 24-vertex path. Its h_4 upper bounds do not establish the maximum over all triangle-free hosts or the paper’s asymptotic claims.

science-triangle-free-diameter-two-degre.rationale: The candidate returns the edge list of a graph on 50 vertices; the evaluator checks that it is triangle-free with diameter at most two and scores the maximum degree, smaller being better. Reviewed source family science_prize_f_diameter_two, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Triangle-free diameter-two graphs on 50 vertices with small maximum degree
evidence.description: construct() -> list of edges [u, v] of a simple graph on vertices 0..49 that is triangle-free and has diameter at most two (every pair adjacent or with a common neighbour). Minimize the maximum degree; the optimum is 7. The Moore bound forces maximum degree at least 7 on 50 vertices, and the Hoffman-Singleton graph attains it, so 7 is optimal.

science-triangles-above-turan-16.rationale: The candidate returns exactly 68 edges on 16 vertices; the evaluator counts the triangles of the graph exactly, and fewer is better. Reviewed source family science_prize_f_triangles_above_turan, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Fewest triangles in graphs with 16 vertices and 68 edges
evidence.description: construct() -> exactly 68 distinct edges [u, v] on vertices 0..15. The score is the exact number of triangles. Minimize; the proven optimum is 32 = t * floor(n/2) with t = 68 - 64. With n = 16 and t = 4 the theorem gives at least 32 triangles, and 32 is attained.

science-triple-systems-matching-two-12.rationale: The candidate returns distinct triples on 12 points; the evaluator checks that no three of them are pairwise disjoint and scores the number of triples. Reviewed source family science_prize_f_matching_two, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Triple systems on 12 points without three disjoint triples
evidence.description: construct() -> list of distinct triples [a, b, c] of distinct points in 0..11 containing no three pairwise disjoint triples. Maximize the number of triples; the proven optimum is 100. For n = 12 and s = 2 the maximum is max{56, 100} = 100.

science-triple-systems-without-k222-16.rationale: The candidate returns distinct triples on 16 points; the evaluator checks that no three disjoint pairs have all eight transversal triples present and scores the number of triples. Reviewed source family science_prize_f_tripartite_triples, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Triple systems on 16 points without the complete 3-partite K(2,2,2)
evidence.description: construct() -> list of distinct triples [a, b, c] of distinct points in 0..15 such that no three disjoint pairs have all eight transversal triples present. science-two-color-four-progression-avoid.rationale: The candidate constructs a 0/1 coloring of an initial segment of the integers with no monochromatic four-term arithmetic progression; the evaluator checks every progression exactly, and the length is maximized. evidence.task_name: Long binary colorings without four-term progressions

science-two-primitive-integer-sets.rationale: The candidate returns a set of integers in 2..256. The evaluator checks that no member divides the product of two other members and scores the set size. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_652, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large integer sets with no two-other-product divisibility
evidence.description: construct() -> nonempty distinct integers in 2..256. For every THREE DISTINCT members a,b,c, require that a does not divide b*c. Maximize cardinality. In particular b and c cannot denote the same member; this convention is part of the finite contract. Only the interval up to 256 is searched. The verifier uses three distinct members, and it does not claim a sharp asymptotic error term or optimal cardinality.

science-uniform-no-singleton-intersectio.rationale: The candidate returns a family of four-element subsets of a 16-element set. The evaluator checks that no two members share exactly one element and scores the family size. Reviewed source family science_prize_c_572, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Large uniform families without singleton intersections
evidence.description: construct() -> 1..1000 distinct four-element subsets of 0..15. No two members may intersect in exactly one element. Maximize the number of members. science-unique-triple-sum-b3-4096.rationale: The candidate constructs at most 80 distinct integers in [1,4096] whose sums of three elements (repetition allowed) are all different; the evaluator checks every triple sum exactly, and the size of the set is maximized. evidence.task_name: Large integer sets with unique triple sums
evidence.description: construct() -> 1..80 distinct positive integers <=n=4096. Every unordered triple, allowing repetitions, must have a different sum. Maximize cardinality. science-van-der-waerden-three-versus-twe.rationale: The candidate returns a two-colouring of 1..N; the evaluator checks exhaustively that one colour has no 3-term and the other no 12-term arithmetic progression and scores N. Reviewed source family science_prize_h_van_der_waerden, area mathematics.

evidence.task_name: Two-colourings avoiding a red 3-term and a blue 12-term progression (w(3,12) = 135)

tdc-admet-ames.rationale: The candidate is a molecular property predictor scored on a held-out TDC ADMET split and compared with the leaderboard. Reviewed source family admet, collection open-problems-2026-11.

evidence.description: Predict whether a compound is mutagenic in the Ames test (1) or not (0) from its molecular structure, given as a SMILES string (endpoint AMES of the Therapeutics Data Commons ADMET benchmark group). The measured compounds are split by molecular scaffold into a training, a validation and a test part. The test part is fixed; the candidate is run five times (seeds 1 to 5), each time with a different division of the other compounds into training and validation. It receives the training and validation compounds with their values and the test compounds without, and returns one prediction per test compound. Each of the five runs is a separate process that receives only these arguments: it cannot read the evaluator's files, start other processes or open network connections, and it has 700 seconds. The score is the area under the ROC curve on the test compounds, averaged over the five runs; higher is better.

methodology.classification_authority: Arena editorial inference from the pinned catalog; these labels are not a taxonomy supplied or certified by the source authors.
methodology.unit: One canonical registered task package (task ID). This snapshot merges 254 upstream aliases; remaining parameter variants and distinct protocols are separate packages. Counts are not counts of unique scientific problems.
methodology.primary_domain: Exactly one primary application domain per package. Classification follows the candidate objective/target, not paper-title keywords or the subject of QA/retrieval documents. Cross-domain connections are discussed in definitions, never counted twice.
methodology.task_type: Exactly one task type per package, describing the candidate operation independently of application domain.
methodology.rules: Ordered first-match rules: explicit scientific targets and mixed-family exceptions, reviewed task groups, defaults for each of 151 source families, then unknown. Conditions within a rule are AND; values within one condition are OR. Historical rule IDs containing unsupported do not override current catalog availability.
methodology.evidence: Annotations retain the matched rule, rationale, task name, description, metric, source family and paper IDs. Exact-ID lists were resolved using catalog/duplicates.json at source commit 5729caa7a3bd4e66c39a447c0d4ee56dc8fa0935; merged predecessors had consistent domain/type assignments. New family classifications review catalog/tasks.json, labels.area, candidate interfaces and catalog/science/*.json at that commit. These are editorial classifications, not endorsements of upstream scientific-importance or open-problem labels.
methodology.percentages: Each domain distribution and each task-type distribution uses all catalog packages as denominator. Largest-remainder rounding to 0.1 percentage point makes each partition sum to 100.0%; ties use taxonomy definition order.
methodology.availability: Executable and unsupported counts preserve source protocol status. Classification neither installs an environment nor establishes runtime readiness, fidelity, reproducibility or Arena conformance.
methodology.papers: Corpus paper counts exclude the 15 supplemental source IDs declared in non_paper_source_ids: SCiEL, Santa 2025 and 13 science collections. This snapshot covers 98 corpus paper IDs and 113 source groups. unique_paper_count is a compatibility alias for source_group_count; label it source groups. Per-group paper_count counts corpus IDs, not independently verified publications. Per-group source_group_count includes supplements; group coverage overlaps.
methodology.families: Family counts exclude null source families. Families can span domains/types and must not be summed across groups.
methodology.coverage: Coverage rows are overlapping indicators, each using the complete package denominator. They are not a distribution and their percentages must not be summed.
methodology.scientific_relevance: why_it_matters describes the modeled function or evaluation operation, not a subjective scientific-importance ranking or a claim that the benchmark produced a discovery.
methodology.refresh: Changing catalog or taxonomy requires rebuilding insights.json. Offline validation compares digests, every assignment and all aggregate totals before serving the Python API.
